Executive Summary
        This report contains specific information regarding the detailed forensic performance testing (outlined 
later in this report) of the energy control measure (ECM) PermaFrost NMR® in two of the many packaged 
roof top units (RTUs) supporting the Electrical Supply Distributor facility in [Texas City].  Patrick Amante, Electrical Supply Distributor Energy 
Solutions, personally witnessed all phases of the testing and data collection. 
The two RTUs comprising this pilot project, one 90,000 
Btu and the other 36,000 Btu, each utilize R-22 
refrigerant and were installed in 1998.  Based on BIN 
data for Houston for all the hours per year over 65 
degrees, the units run 5,790 hours each year.  
Immediately following the baseline testing, the units 
were each treated with the proper amount of 
PermaFrost NMR® product specially formulated for 
R-22 DX systems.
Since there were no other ECM’s going on during this 
pilot project, the improvement in efficiency and 
restored capacity gained directly at the units was 
solely attributable to the PermaFrost NMR® ECM.  
Despite much lower than design air flow across the 
coils, both RTUs now provide colder supply air and 
more Btu’s while using less watts per ton.  This greater 
operational efficiency is due to the restoration of the 
heat transfer ability of the evaporator and condenser 
coils, less metal-to-metal friction and improved 
refrigerant flow.

Product Brief
         PermaFrost NMR® is a multi-patented nanotechnology surface chemistry Energy Control 
Measure (ECM) that uses Nucleo Molecular Regenerative (NMR®) technology as its core agent. A 
sustainable, one-time treatment with no down time required, PermaFrost NMR® lasts for the remaining 
life of any type of system in which it is installed – DX (direct expansion air and chilled water systems), 
chillers (screw, reciprocating, scroll and centrifugal), heat pumps and ice making equipment.  
Specialized applications include computer room cooling and dehumidification systems, chiller plants 
(water and ice production applications), domestic and industrial refrigeration (ammonia low and ultra 
low temperature), air-cooled single application water chillers and split and package rooftop HVAC 
equipment.
The direct benefits of PermaFrost NMR® are improved cooling performance, increased capacity and 
improved refrigerant velocity – all of which allows a system to achieve set point temperatures in a more 
rapid fashion which reduces system loading and operating periods.  The indirect benefits resulting 
from the enhanced thermodynamic characteristics following treatment include reduced run time, less 
kW hours used, less amp draw at the compressor per ton, less metallic wear, longer overall equipment 
life and a reduced carbon footprint for Electrical Supply Distributor.

Engineering Conclusions
The client, Douglas North, Facilities Management Director, Major Tire Manufacturer [Eastern Cape Location] Plant was consulted 
regarding this equipment after the avoided energy reporting period (post analysis) and the following 
observations were discussed.
 
        The evaporator coil has some visual mold growth on the leaving airside of the aluminum fins. This is 
causing some additional pressure drop across the tube and fin evaporator.
 
 2     The blower drive components are not performing at the proper RPM due to the degradation of drive 
sheaves. Once corrected, the belts should also be replaced. This is causing a reduction in the area of available 
delivered cubic feet of supply air per minute (CFM). Please note that this condition was present during the 
baseline data period and was not corrected until after this pilot analysis was to be completed. Now that the 
pilot testing period has ended, this correction should commence.
 2     Compressor number one (1) was recently replaced and is now showing evidence of overheating. There 
is a refrigerant leak emitting from the capillary tubing connecting the compressor to its respective safety 
switches. Evidence of this refrigerant oil can be seen inside of the pressure controls section cabinet.
        There are four segregated sections of evaporator coils that are joined together creating one evaporator. 
Compressor #1 serves two of the circuits and the other two circuits are served by compressor #2. Each 
section of the respective circuits is comprised of two thermostatic expansion valves (TXV) for each 
compressor. Each of these TXV’s had a different superheat. This should be corrected in a timely manner. The 
evaporator should be cleaned and the belts and sheaves should be corrected before this adjustment is 
initiated.

Technology Brief
The Problem
During normal operation, heat transfer surfaces in HVAC systems can become less efficient over time. This thermal degradation reduces the ability of the system to transfer heat effectively, thus reducing overall efficiency. Almost every piece of HVAC equipment in the world experiences some degree of thermal efficiency loss over its operating life. Independent studies from the American Society of Heating, 
Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE) have concluded that thermal inefficiency can increase the 
electricity consumption of any HVAC system by up to 30% within the first five years of equipment life.  
The Solution
        PermaFrost NMR® is a nanotechnology that uses Nucleo Molecular Regenerative® (NMR™) 
technology as its core agent to eliminate and reverse the effects of thermal inefficiency on HVAC equipment.  A 
one-time treatment of PermaFrost NMR® will provide thermal efficiency protection for the remaining life of any 
refrigerant system. The manufacturer of PermaFrost NMR®, Powertron Global®, has installed and tested 
PermaFrost NMR® in over 115,000 HVAC and refrigeration systems around the world and has experienced 
energy reduction in direct expansion (DX), Chiller (screw, reciprocating, scroll and centrifugal), heat pumps, 
and ice making equipment. Specialized applications include computer room cooling and dehumidification 
systems, chiller plants (water and ice production applications), domestic and industrial refrigeration 
(ammonia low and ultra low temperature), air-cooled single application water chillers, and split and 
package rooftop HVACR equipment.
The direct benefits of PermaFrost NMR® include improved cooling performance, increased capacity and 
improved refrigerant velocity--all of which allow systems to achieve set point temperatures more quickly, 
which reduces compressor operating times. The indirect benefits resulting from the enhanced 
thermodynamic characteristics following treatment include reduced run time, fewer kilowatt hours used, 
less amp draw at the compressor, longer equipment life and reduced carbon footprint.

Engineering Notes
According to AHRI (American Refrigeration Research Institute) which is the governing body of all HVACR 
equipment sold nationwide, HVACR capacity is categorized by a standard set of parameters before their 
capacity is advertised to the public. The standard for chillers maintains proper design flow in the 
evaporator and condenser as well as static entering temperatures of 80 degrees for the condenser and 55 
degrees for the evaporator. Lower temperatures than this will create the effect of increased capacity such as 
those that were present during this test.  Additionally, increased flow with lower temperatures will create a 
false positive of a chillers’ capacity. This is evident in the loss of performance and the inability of the chiller 
to produce the design delta T within the heat exchange vessels (evaporator and condenser).

Important Manufacturer's Note
     PermaFrost® is designed to allow the system to achieve thermostat set points faster thereby allowing 
the unit to cycle off or cycle down to provide the greatest energy savings.  The proper way to measure the full 
benefits of PermaFrost® include allowing the system to cycle on and off normally and measure kWh use 
over time.
 
Significantly greater energy savings are measurable when the process of recycling air (cooling cooler air) 
and measuring kWh use over time are included in the test.  This test is designed to measure efficiency 
improvemnet only when the unit is running.  This test does not take into account the exponential benifit of 
coolong cooler air and the full energy savings derived from producing colder air.  Increased cooling capacity 
allows the system to reach the thermostat set point temperature quicker.  The energy savings not accounted 
for in this test is the energy saved due to reduced runtime.  
 
With PermaFrost® installed the unit will acieve thermostat temperature setpoint faster and remain off for 
longer periods of time saving energy.

Executive Summary
         This report contains specific information regarding the installation of the energy control measure 
(ECM) PermaFrost NMR® in one of the two main HVAC units supporting the County Law Enforcement A MD Police 
Department located at [Government Facility Address], [LOCATION REDACTED], MD. Detailed forensic performance testing 
(outlined later in this report) was performed on the nominal 26-ton split system outfitted with one 
compressor using R22 refrigerant. Following testing, the unit was treated with the proper amount and type 
of the PermaFrost NMR® technology specially formulated for these types of systems.  Measurement and 
Verification (M&V) was conducted pre-installation and post-gestation.
 
The improvement in efficiency and restored capacity gained directly at the unit was solely attributable to the 
PermaFrost NMR® ECM. This is a result of the reversal of thermal inefficiency on heat exchange surfaces.  
Following treatment with the PermaFrost NMR® technology, the unit showed an effective net average 
15.9% reduction in kW/ton based on the exact capacity measured in the baseline M&V and the post 
gestation M&V. With the 26-ton unit operating at full load with all VAV boxes open at 100%, the system 
showed an average 1.3% reduction in kW consumption while simultaneously producing an increase in 
capacity of 3.8 tons. This 17.3% average capacity increase from the baseline performance level led to an 
effective average increase in COP of 19.4%. All of these factors directly correlate to what County Law Enforcement A 
will realize in energy savings as they operate this system in the future under the same parameters.
Following treatment with the PermaFrost NMR® technology, the system showed an average 2% reduction 
in amp draw while at the same time the unit was doing much more work. This is illustrated by the 21% 
increase in the enthalpy delta, which is a critical HVAC measurement used to determine the 
thermodynamic enhancement brought about by the PermaFrost NMR® ECM.  The result of the ECM 
improvement is an ROI to County Law Enforcement A that is measured in months. The tables of data are available for 
review at the end of this report. Financial calculations determining the true ROI are proprietary to [County A] 
County under separate cover.

Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol
The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP) was utilized in the 
development of this report. The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), The American Society of Heating, 
Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and The Efficiency Valuation Organization 
(EVO) accept the IPMVP as a global methodology for determining the effectiveness of energy conservation 
methods and products.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize. They 
are options A, B, C and D.  Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report. Option B is 
defined as: All parameter measurements with the boundary of the ECM (PermaFrost NMR®) as the single 
source of measurement. Savings are determined by field measurement of the energy use of the ECM 
affected equipment or system and any performance enhancements versus the baseline data.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period.  For the boundary utilized for Option B short-term 
measurements are very useful as data when the variables are contained. The savings are calculated by 
short-term measurements of baseline and energy reporting period (post), and /or engineering computations 
using measurements of proxies of energy use.

Purpose of Energy Eﬃciency Study
The purpose of this study is to verify the industry wide problem of 
efficiency loss in HVAC/R as projected by ASHRAE research and to 
quantify the amount of money wasted due to this loss. Many 
industry leading organizations including ASHRAE project that all 
HVAC/R units degrade in capacity and efficiency as they age. 
Thermal degradation is caused by a phenomenon that is present in 
all HVAC/R equipment that operates as a vapor compression cycle 
associated with refrigerant and compressor lubricant. This thermal 
degradation is well documented by the HVAC/R industry and the 
original equipment manufacturers (OEM’s). Thermal degradation 
prevents units from operating at the original design efficiency, which 
leads to excessive run-times and additional kWh consumption.
The CRAC systems in this study are representative of a great 
majority of the portfolio of equipment operated by Tech Company A. If thermal degradation is 
present in these systems it is present in the entire inventory of equipment. Energy waste can be calculated based 
on this equipment (portfolio representation) and then accurately extrapolated across the entire inventory of 
equipment.

Following a diagnostic examination to determine the operational condition of the CRAC systems was satisfactory, Baseline 
M&V data was collected and recorded by the M&V team. Approximately 400+ runtime hours after installation of the 
ECM, the M&V team returned to take Post M&V measurements in the identical fashion as in the baseline. The delta of 
these measurements and associated calculations show the amount of capacity restored.
The following baseline IPMVP data points were recorded on Q2 2106. The two systems were then treated with 
PermaFrost NMR® on the same day and allowed to run normally until Q3 2016 to ensure the patented surface science 
nanotechnology had ample time to seat into all the metal surfaces of the heat exchangers. All measurements were taken at 
similar incoming air temperatures however the outdoor air temperature in the post was 6 degrees F warmer (93 deg F vs. 99 
deg F). The manufacturer provided a computerized load selection chart to illustrate that for every degree higher in ambient 
dry bulb temperature the system would lose approximately .60% of capacity (please see Appendix A). The total loss of 
capacity per degree equated to 3.61% and then this percentage was added to each system's measured total capacity in the 
post. For CRAC #59 an additional .97 tons was added to the measured total calculated capacity and for CRAC #60  an 
additional .69 tons was added.
Normalization of input kW (amperage specifically) was also employed in order to account for the 6 degrees F higher 
ambient dry bulb temperature. Compressors account for 70% of the total amperage consumed which is also true with these 
systems (please see Appendix A). The following formula was used: Actual Measured Amps x (Actual Measured Amps x 
0.7 x % increase in Ambient DB Temp). For CRAC #59 the post-measured amperage of 46.2 was reduced to 44.1. For 
CRAC #60 the post-measured amperage of 47.5 was reduced to 45.4 amps. These new amperage numbers were entered into 
standard electrical formula of V x A x PF x 1.732/1000 in order to normalize system kW.

Executive Summary
         This report contains specific information regarding the installation of the energy control measure 
(ECM) PermaFrost NMR® in [Brazil Location] for International Bank A. Detailed forensic performance testing 
(outlined later in this report) was performed on 8 DX units ranging from 15 to 40 tons in size. It was 
determined to demonstrate the performance of the product in both administrative and branch type 
buildings.
Immediately following the baseline testing, all the units were treated with the proper amount and type of 
PermaFrost NMR® product formulated for R-22 DX and R-438A systems. Since there were no other ECM’s 
going on during this pilot project, the improvement in efficiency and restored capacity gained directly at the 
units is solely attributable to the PermaFrost NMR® ECM. The unit(s) now provide cooler/drier supply air 
while using less power. This greater operational efficiency is due to the restoration of the heat transfer 
ability of the evaporator and condenser coils.

Product Brief
         PermaFrost NMR® is a multi-patented nanotechnology surface chemistry Energy Control Measure 
(ECM) that uses Nucleo Molecular Regenerative (NMR) technology as its core agent. A sustainable, 
one-time treatment with no down time required, PermaFrost NMR® lasts for the remaining life of any 
type of system in which it is installed. Examples of the types of commercial HVACR systems and 
equipment that PermaFrost NMR® has proven success with are direct expansion air systems (DX); 
chilled water systems (both flooded and DX; air and water cooled); ice making equipment; ammonia 
refrigeration plants (single compressor and cascade) and variable refrigerant flow (VRF) designs. The 
equipment utilized in these systems within our expanding portfolio of clients includes centrifugal (single 
and multi-stage), scroll, reciprocating and screw configurations.
The direct benefits of PermaFrost NMR® are improved cooling performance, increased capacity and 
improved refrigerant velocity – all of which allow systems to achieve set point temperatures in a more 
rapid fashion which reduces compressor operating periods. The indirect benefits resulting from the 
enhanced thermodynamic characteristics following treatment include reduced run time, less kW hours 
used, less amp draw at the compressor, longer equipment life cycle time and a reduced carbon footprint 
for International Bank A.

Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol
The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP) was utilized in the 
development of this report. The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), American Society of Heating, 
Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and The Efficiency Valuation Organization 
(EVO) accept the IPMVP as a global methodology for determining the effectiveness of energy conservation 
methods and products.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize. They 
are options A, B, C and D.  Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report. Retrofit Isolation 
(Option B) is defined as: All parameter measurement with the boundary of the ECM (PermaFrost NMR®) as 
the single source of measurement. Savings are determined by field measurement of the energy use of the 
energy conservation method affected equipment or system and any performance enhancements versus the 
baseline data.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period.  For the boundary utilized for Option B short-term 
measurements are very useful as data when the variables are contained. The savings are calculated by 
short-term measurements of baseline and reporting period energy, and /or engineering computations using 
measurements of proxies of energy use.

Conclusion / Notes
The nominal capacity for the HVAC units in this report were determined by the manufacturer at the 
conditions of incoming condenser water at 85 degree F and entering evaporator air temperature of 80 
degrees F. The conditions during this M&V procedures were less than the design parameters, which 
accounted for the capacities well above design even before the ECM PermaFrost NMR® was installed. 
These conditions were present in both baseline and post (Energy Reporting Period) periods therefore the 
improvements PermaFrost NMR® brought about are sound and scientifically verified.
The runtime and electric energy cost (0,43R$ with all Brazilian taxes) was informed by [Bank Representative]  (from Branches department) and [Bank Representative] (for Administrative department) and moreover that 
consideration was taken in the equipments 60% of the total runtime only.
The total cost of PermaFrost NMR® was calculated based on the price with all the Brazilian taxation, as well 
as, trading company costs included which reached out the value per unit of $ 205,8USD.
Following the treatment of PermaFrost NMR®, the installed units (8) showed a substantial reduction in 
Watts/energy of 47.1%, the average improvement in COP was 44.7%, the average overall system efficiency 
and Btuh capacity improvements were 38.0% and the total restored capacity was 54.5 tons.
In conclusion, regarding the ECO efficient/sustainable respect to this project International Bank A saved the 
environment 149 metric tons of green house gas emissions -carbon dioxide- as well as saved 210,592 kWh of 
power.

Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol
The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP) was utilized in the 
development of this report. The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), The American Society of Heating, 
Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and The Efficiency Valuation Organization 
(EVO) accept the IPMVP as a global methodology for determining the effectiveness of energy conservation 
methods and products.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize. They 
are options A, B, C and D.  Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report. Option B is 
defined as: All parameter measurements with the boundary of the ECM (PermaFrost NMR®) as the single 
source of measurement. Savings are determined by field measurement of the energy use of the ECM 
affected equipment or system and any performance enhancements versus the baseline data.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period.  For the boundary utilized for Option B short-term 
measurements are very useful as data when the variables are contained. The savings are calculated by 
short-term measurements of baseline and energy reporting period (post), and /or engineering computations 
using measurements of proxies of energy use.

Purpose of Energy Eﬃciency Study
The purpose of this study is to verify the industry wide problem of efficiency loss in HVAC/R as projected by 
ASHRAE research and to quantify the amount of money wasted due to this loss. Many industry leading 
organizations including ASHRAE project that all HVAC/R units degrade in capacity and efficiency as they age. 
Thermal degradation is caused by a phenomenon that is present in all HVAC/R equipment that operates as a 
vapor compression cycle associated with refrigerant and compressor lubricant. This thermal degradation is well 
documented by the HVAC/R industry and the original equipment manufacturers (OEM’s). Thermal 
degradation prevents units from operating at the original design efficiency, which leads to excessive run-times 
and additional kWh consumption.

Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol
The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP) was utilized in the 
development of this report. The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), The American Society of Heating, 
Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and The Efficiency Valuation Organization 
(EVO) accept the IPMVP as a global methodology for determining the effectiveness of energy conservation 
methods and products.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize. They 
are options A, B, C and D.  Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report. Option B is 
defined as: All parameter measurements with the boundary of the ECM (PermaFrost NMR®) as the single 
source of measurement. Savings are determined by field measurement of the energy use of the ECM 
affected equipment or system and any performance enhancements versus the baseline data.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period.  For the boundary utilized for Option B short-term 
measurements are very useful as data when the variables are contained. The savings are calculated by 
short-term measurements of baseline and energy reporting period (post), and /or engineering computations 
using measurements of proxies of energy use.

Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol
The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP) was utilized in the 
development of this report. The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), The American Society of Heating, 
Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and The Efficiency Valuation Organization 
(EVO) accept the IPMVP as a global methodology for determining the effectiveness of energy conservation 
methods and products.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize. They 
are options A, B, C and D.  Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report. Option B is 
defined as: All parameter measurements with the boundary of the ECM as the single source of 
measurement. Savings are determined by field measurement of the energy use of the ECM affected 
equipment or system and any performance enhancements versus the baseline data.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period.  For the boundary utilized for Option B short-term 
measurements are very useful as data when the variables are contained. The savings are calculated by 
short-term measurements of baseline and energy reporting period (post), and /or engineering computations 
using measurements of proxies of energy use.

Purpose of Energy Eﬃciency Study
Thermal degradation is well documented by the American Society of Heating, Refrigeration and Air 
Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE) and the original equipment manufacturers (OEM’s). It is a major cause of 
capacity loss in Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration (HVACR) systems, preventing them 
from operating at the original design efficiency. 
The purpose of this efficiency study is to verify the effectiveness of the PermaFrost NMR® Energy Conservation 
Measure (ECM) in Grocery Chain A Regional Grocery Chain HVACR systems and document the performance improvements and future 
energy cost reductions associated with the same.  
Summary Results
This comprehensive report contains specific information regarding the 
performance profile of a 5-ton Roof Top Unit (RTU) and one medium 
temperature refrigeration rack system supporting the Grocery Chain A Regional Grocery Chain 
facility in [Location].

39,420. Combined, the systems also showed a 23.3% reduction in kW/ton 
and an 20.3% reduction in kWh usage. These efficiency improvements 
equate to an Initial Payback Period (IPP) of the ECM project for Grocery Chain A 
of 12.4 months and a corresponding Internal Rate of Return (IRR) of 
96.6%

Energy Conservation Method (ECM)
The content detailed in both phases of this report will first demonstrate the ability of the respective systems to 
perform prior to the PermaFrost NMR® (ECM) being installed, as well as illustrate the amount of thermal 
degradation each has developed over time due in large part to thermal degradation within the heat exchangers.
 
Following a diagnostic examination of each of the pilot systems to determine their operational condition was 
satisfactory; baseline M&V data was collected and recorded by the M&V team. 
Approximately five weeks after installation of PermaFrost NMR®, the M&V team returned to uninstall all the 
monitoring equipment after verifying with Clima-Check that the data taken during the pilot was satisfactory. 
Regarding the RTU, the team was also careful to return for post measurements on a similar weather day to the 
baseline so the effects on the condensing coils would be consistent. The delta of these measurements and the 
associated calculations demonstrate the amount of improvement the ECM had across both systems.

• kWh= kW * Runtime Hours

• Amps = direct collection showing amount of work the compressor is doing

• kW/Ton = kW consumed / actual measured tonnage

RTU Testing Methodology
For this portion of the pilot, measurement data was collected prior to the RTU being treated with the 
PermaFrost NMR® ECM on 6 June 2014. PermaFrost NMR® was then allowed to work for a period of at least 
400+ hours before the post measurements were taken on a similar weather day and then compared to the 
baseline data.
  
To reduce the impact of the store variables on the data, care was taken to have similar outside air temperatures 
affecting the ability of the condensing coils to reject heat as well as similar entering wet bulb and dry bulb 
temperatures. With these three conditions accomplished and the boundary of the test being the RTU itself, the 
confidence level in the resulting data in very high. 
For the RTU phase, the comparisons included testing conducted on the days listed below:
Baseline -  Friday 6 June, Outside Air Temp of 75°, Entering DB of 71.4°, Entering WB of 56.9° 
Post - Friday 1 August, Outside Air Temp of 75°, Entering DB of 70.3°, Entering WB of 56.7°
The boundary of the testing was the RTU and nothing else; therefore confidence in the accuracy of the 
performance calculations is very high.

Rack-B Refrigeration Testing Methodology
For this portion of the pilot, measurement data was collected using the Clima-Check Performance Analyzer 
prior to Rack-B being treated with the PermaFrost NMR® ECM on 18 June 2014. The ECM was then allowed to 
work for a period of at least 400+ hours before baseline data was then compared to the post data on similar 
weather days. 
To reduce the impact of the store variables on the data, two similar periods of time on similar days of the week 
with similar in-store and outside air wet and dry bulb temperatures were chosen to compare refrigeration 
performance before and after the ECM. These comparisons included:
Baseline - Friday 13 June, 75° Average Outdoor Air Temp, 8AM – 8PM (full day of operations)  
Post - Friday 18 July, 78° Average Outdoor Air Temp, 8AM – 8PM (full day of operations)
The boundary of the testing was the Rack-B medium temperature compressors and nothing else; therefore 
confidence in the accuracy of the performance calculations is very high.

Testing Methodology
The M&V team used the aforementioned IPMVP methodology to capture the performance and energy use of 
the three pilot systems. First, after verifying the amount of air flowing across the evaporator coils in the DX 
equipment or water flowing through the evaporator barrel of the chiller before beginning each pilot phase, the 
subsequent measurements used in the efficiency calculations were collected and compiled in accordance with 
Option B of the IPMVP. This Protocol was developed by experts in the international community to provide a 
consistent method for analyzing HVAC/R system performance. Baseline measurements for the chiller and WIC 
were taken on Q4 2015. Post measurements for these same two systems were taken on January 6, 
2016. The baseline for the split system was taken on this same day while the post measurements were taken on 
January 26, 2016.
 
The results presented below were formulated by entering the data into the following thermodynamic 
engineering formulas:
 
• kW = Volts * Amps * Power Factor * Sq Rt 3 /1000 (for 3-Phase) 
 
• kW/ton = Actual Measured Energy / Actual Measured Capacity 
 
• Coefficient of Performance (COP) = 12 / (kW/ton) /3.412
 
• Tons of Cooling = (Measured CFM * 4.5 * Enthalpy Delta T) / 12,000 BTU
 
• BTUs (Refrigeration) = (Airflow * 1.08 * Temp Δ)

HVAC/R Eﬃciency Report
Purpose of Energy Eﬃciency Study
The purpose of this study is to verify the industry wide problem of efficiency loss in HVAC/R as projected by 
ASHRAE research and to quantify the amount of money wasted due to this loss. Many industry leading 
organizations including ASHRAE project that all HVAC/R units degrade in capacity and efficiency as they age. 
Thermal degradation is caused by a phenomenon that is present in all HVAC/R equipment that operates as a 
vapor compression cycle associated with refrigerant and compressor lubricant. This thermal degradation is well 
documented by the HVACR industry and the original equipment manufacturers (OEM’s). Thermal degradation 
prevents units from operating at the original design efficiency, which leads to excessive run-times and additional 
kWh consumption.
The chillers in this study (pictured below) are 
representative of a great majority of the 
portfolio of equipment operated by State Military A. If thermal degradation is 
present in these chillers it is present in the 
entire inventory of equipment. Energy waste 
can be calculated based on this equipment 
(portfolio representation) and then accurately 
extrapolated across the entire inventory of 
equipment.

Process
This report contains specific information regarding the current performance profile of two chillers that support 
the Military Installation [Facility Code REDACTED] in [LOCATION REDACTED], LA 
Detailed performance testing (outlined later in this report) was performed on the pilot chillers before and after 
the installation of the ECM to determine the impact on the three key elements that greatly affect the HVAC 
power bill as they relate to the original design specifications:
 
 
1.  The cooling capacity the chillers produce after 10 years in service, before and after the 
 
     administration of the ECM. 
 
2.  The actual cost of power required to produce the amount of cooling tons the chillers can deliver as 
 
     reflected in the kW/ton measurement, before and after the administration of the ECM. 
 
3.  The thermal dynamic ability of the chillers to perform in relation to operational design, before and 
 
     after the administration of the ECM.
Methodology
The measurements used in the efficiency calculations were collected and compiled in accordance with the 
IPMVP (International Measurement and Verification Protocol) framework. The team consisted Captain Jeremy 
A. Futrell and [Infrastructure Consultant] & [Client Representative] of Infrastructure Contractor. 
Notes
The equipment tested (2) RTAA-100 air-cooled chillers manufactured by HVAC Equipment Manufacturer.  Both the baseline and post measurement 
s were taken with outside air temperatures of 81-82 degrees.  
The flow rate through the evaporators were nearly identical in the baseline and post and the return chilled water entering 
the chiller in the baseline and post were identical so no adjustments were made.
The boundary of the testing was the chillers and nothing else; therefore confidence in the accuracy of the performance 
calculations is very high.

Energy Conservation Method (ECM)
The content detailed in this report will first demonstrate the ability of the pilot chillers to perform prior to the 
PermaFrost NMR® (ECM) being installed, as well as illustrate the amount of thermal degradation due in large 
part to thermal degradation within the heat exchangers.
 
The following report produces the utilization of the IPMVP as the M&V plan. 
The results were formulated by entering the data into the following thermodynamic engineering formulas:
 
• kW = Volts * Amps * Power Factor of 1.47/1000 (for 3-Phase) 
 
• kW/Ton = kW / Actual Tonnage 
 
• Coefficient of Performance (COP) = (12 / kW per ton /3.412)
 
• Actual Cooling Tons per Hour = Evaporator GPM X 8.34 * 60 * Chilled Water Delta T / 12,000 BTU 
 
• Refrigerant Approach = Supply Water Temp – Saturated Evaporator Temp (CH) 
 
Notes
Following a diagnostic examination to determine the operational condition of the chillers were satisfactory, Baseline 
M&V data was collected and recorded by the M&V team. 400+ runtime hours after installation of the ECM, the M&V 
team returned on a very similar weather day to the Baseline to take Post M&V measurements in the identical fashion as 
in the Baseline and at the almost identicle outdoor air temperature. The delta of these measurements and associated 
calculations show the amount of capacity restored.
The following IPMVP data points were recorded on April 22/23, 2015 using recently calibrated by NIST (National 
Institutes of Standards and Technology) to insure GPM measurement accuracy. The remaining measurements were 
taken directly from the chiller’s control panel. The chiller was then treated with PermaFrost NMR® on the same day and 
allowed to run normally until Q2 2015 to ensure the patented surface science nanotechnology had ample time to seat 
into all the metal surfaces of the heat exchangers. All measurements were taken at identical incoming water temperatures 
as well as almost identical outdoor air temperatures. [Personnel Name], Gregory and Sunba of the State Military A, 
witnessed the collection of the data.

Executive Summary
         This report contains specific information regarding the installation of the energy control measure 
(ECM) PermaFrost NMR® in Oak Brook, IL for Data Center Provider Data Center. Detailed forensic performance testing 
(outlined later in this report) was performed on a 30 ton Liebert DX unit. 
Immediately following the baseline testing, both stages were treated with the proper amount and type of 
PermaFrost NMR® product formulated for R-22 DX systems. Since there were no other ECM’s going on 
during this pilot project, the improvement in efficiency and restored capacity gained directly at the units is 
solely attributable to the PermaFrost NMR® ECM. The unit(s) now provides cooler/drier supply air while 
using less power. This greater operational efficiency is due to the restoration of the heat transfer ability of 
the evaporator and condenser coils.
Following treatment of PermaFrost NMR® the unit showed a substantial increase in coil capacity of 179,434 
Btuh or 47.1% improvement overall system efficiency. This restored capacity equates to 15 tons. The unit 
also showed a substantial reduction in total Watts of 31.8% and an 46.6% improvement in COP. 
Additionally, the unit showed an 33.5% improvement in Enthalpy Delta, which is another measurable way 
to view the thermodynamic enhancement of the PermaFrost NMR® ECM. 
The result of the ECM improvements is an ROI to customer of just 6.3 months. The tables of data and 
financial calculations are available for review at the end of this report.

Product Brief
         PermaFrost NMR® is a multi-patented nanotechnology surface chemistry Energy Control Measure 
(ECM) that uses Nucleo Molecular Regenerative (NMR) technology as its core agent. A sustainable, 
one-time treatment with no down time required, PermaFrost NMR® lasts for the remaining life of any

The Problem
During normal operation, heat transfer surfaces in HVAC systems can become less efficient over time. This thermal degradation reduces the ability of the system to transfer heat effectively, thus reducing overall efficiency.  Almost every piece of HVAC equipment in the world experiences some degree of thermal efficiency loss over its operating life. Independent studies from the American Society of Heating, 
Refrigeration & Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE) have concluded that thermal inefficiency can increase the 
electricity consumption of any HVAC system by up to 30% within the first five years of the equipment’s life.  
Product Brief
         PermaFrost NMR® is a nanotechnology that uses Nucleo Molecular Regenerative (NMR®) 
technology as its core agent to eliminate and reverse the effects of thermal inefficiency on HVAC equipment.  A 
one-time treatment of PermaFrost NMR® will provide thermal efficiency protection for the remaining life of any 
refrigerant system.  The manufacturer of  PermaFrost NMR®, Powertron Global®, has installed and 
tested PermaFrost NMR® in over 108,000 HVAC and refrigeration systems around the world and has 
experienced energy reduction in direct expansion (DX), chiller (screw, reciprocating, scroll and 
centrifugal), heat pumps, and ice making equipment. Specialized applications include computer room 
cooling and dehumidification systems, chiller plants (water and ice production applications), domestic 
and industrial refrigeration (ammonia low and ultra low temperature), air-cooled single application 
water chillers, and split and package rooftop HVACR equipment.
The direct benefits of PermaFrost NMR® include improved cooling performance, increased capacity and 
improved refrigerant velocity – all of which allow systems to achieve set point temperatures more 
quickly, which reduces compressor operating times. The indirect benefits resulting from the enhanced 
thermodynamic characteristics following treatment include reduced run time, fewer kilowatt-hours 
used, less amp draw at the compressor, longer equipment life and reduced carbon footprint.

HVAC/R Eﬃciency Report
Purpose of Energy Eﬃciency Study
The purpose of this study is to verify the industry wide problem of efficiency loss in HVAC/R as projected by 
ASHRAE research and to quantify the amount of money wasted due to this loss. Many industry leading 
organizations including ASHRAE project that all HVAC/R units degrade in capacity and efficiency as they age. 
Thermal degradation is caused by a phenomenon that is present in all HVAC/R equipment that operates as a 
vapor compression cycle associated with refrigerant and compressor lubricant. This thermal degradation is well 
documented by the HVAC/R industry and the original equipment manufacturers (OEM’s). Thermal 
degradation prevents units from operating at the original design efficiency, which leads to excessive run-times 
and additional kWh consumption.

Hotel Properties. If thermal degradation is 
present in this chiller it is present in the entire 
inventory of equipment. Energy waste can be 
calculated based on this equipment (portfolio 
representation) and then accurately 
extrapolated across the entire inventory of 
equipment.

The content detailed in this report will first demonstrate the ability of the pilot chiller to perform prior to the 
PermaFrost NMR® (ECM) being installed, as well as illustrate the amount of thermal degradation due in large 
part to thermal degradation within the heat exchangers.
 
The following report produces the utilization of the IPMVP as the M&V plan. 
The results were formulated by entering the data into the following thermodynamic engineering formulas:
 
• kW = Volts * Amps * Power Factor of 1.47/1000 (for 3-Phase)

ECM Product Brief
PermaFrost NMR® is a multi-patented surface science nanotechnology that uses Nucleo Molecular Regenerative 
(NMR®) technology as its core agent. A sustainable, one-time installation with no down time required, PermaFrost 
NMR® lasts for the remaining life of any type of climate control system in which it is installed. The direct beneﬁts of 
PermaFrost NMR® are improved cooling efﬁciency and increased capacity.
Methodology
After verifying the amount of air ﬂowing across the evaporator coils before beginning each pilot, the subsequent 
measurements used in the efﬁciency calculations were collected using AHRI Standards 210/240 and compiled in 
accordance with Option B of the IPMVP (International Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol) framework.
The results presented below were formulated by entering the data into the following thermodynamic 
engineering formulas:
 
• kW = (Volts * Amps * Power Factor * Sq Rt of 3) /1000 (for 3-Phase)
 
• kW/ton = Actual Measured Energy / Actual Measured Capacity
 
• Coefﬁcient of Performance (COP) = 12 / (kW/ton) / 3.412
 
• Actual Cooling Capacity per Hour = (Measured CFM * 4.5 * Enthalpy Delta T) / 12,000 BTU

• Coefficient of Performance (COP) = (12 / kW per ton /3.412)
• Actual Cooling Tons/Hour = Evap GPM X 8.34 * 60 * Chilled Water Delta T / 12,000 BTU

From August to October 2015, Energy Efﬁcient Technologies, LLC (EET) and Powertron Global (PTG), conducted a 
joint pilot project on three Regional Convenience Store Chain stores located in and around [LOCATION REDACTED], Utah.  A fourth store (Hurricane Store

unrelated to the project involving one of the two main roof top units (RTUs). The primary purpose of this pilot 
project was to demonstrate the effectiveness of implementing PermaFrost NMR® technology into the HVAC and 
refrigeration systems located in each of the stores.  In addition to PermaFrost NMR®, a power factor technology 
called Circuit Master was also included in the pilot to ascertain its feasibility in future Regional Convenience Store Chain Adventure Store 
applications.
 
In order to provide conclusive results demonstrating the cost savings of the aforementioned energy conservation 
measures (ECMs), EET installed utility grade meters with logging capabilities to monitor only the HVAC and 
refrigeration power demand and energy consumption in each store. Baseline (pre) data was collected for two 
weeks before implementing the technologies on August 21st.  Results from power factor correction can be 
noticed immediately so their effect was calculated in the two days immediately preceding and following 
implementation of the Circuit Master devices at the electrical panel.  PermaFrost NMR® requires a minimum of 
350-400 hours of operation on the two rooftops units (RTUs) and multiple refrigeration units supporting each of 
the Regional Convenience Store Chain Adventure Stores before maximum savings are generated.  For this reason, the post data was 
collected after 30 September 2015 yielding the results summarized in subsequent sections. 
The HVAC and refrigeration equipment in this study are representative of a great majority of the portfolio of 
equipment operated by Regional Convenience Store Chain in their Adventure Stores. If thermal degradation is present in this pilot 
equipment, it is present in the entire inventory of Regional Convenience Store Chain cooling equipment. Energy savings calculations based 
on the improvement demonstrated in the pilot equipment (portfolio representation) can then be accurately 
extrapolated across the entire inventory of equipment.

ECM Descriptions
PermaFrost NMR®
Even though the HVAC units at these locations appear to be in good
working condition, there is still an opportunity for energy savings.
All HVAC equipment experiences thermal degradation over time as internal surfaces
of heat exchangers lose their optimal thermal transfer characteristics. This
thermal inefficiency can increase electricity consumption by up to 30% within the
first five years of the equipment's life, resulting in reduced capacity, lower
efficiency, and higher operating costs.
PermaFrost NMR® addresses this degradation by creating a permanent thermal metal coating
on the internal surfaces of the coil system. This coating conditions the metal surfaces,
improving volumetric heat transfer properties and restoring capacity, all while also
protecting against corrosion. Working together, the kilowatt consumption of 
your HVAC system is reduced signiﬁcantly, lowering the cost to produce each ton of cooling. The installation of 
PermaFrost NMR® does not require any additional hardware, maintenance or downtime for installation, and will 
last for the life of the unit.
Circuit Master®
Circuit Master is a product that blocks distortions in electrical power above and 
below the normal signal range and contains line ﬁlter capacitors to improve 
power factor.  This allows induction power equipment such as HVAC, 
refrigeration, motors and pumps to use less energy.  Equipment lifespan is also 
increased and maintenance costs are reduced. This equipment is installed at 
the disconnect for each machine.

Executive Summary
         This report contains specific information regarding the installation of the energy control measure 
(ECM) PermaFrost NMR® at the Major Spice Manufacturer & Company facility located in [LOCATION REDACTED], MD.  Detailed

package unit using R22 refrigerant serving the 4th floor of the facility.  Following testing, the unit was 
treated with the proper amount and type of PermaFrost NMR® product formulated for DX systems.
  
The substantial improvement in efficiency and restored capacity gained directly at the unit was solely 
attributable to the PermaFrost NMR® ECM.  The unit now provides cooler supply air with greater efficiency 
due to the restoration of the heat transfer ability of the evaporator and condenser coils, both of which have a 
direct correlation to an increase in the number of Btuh the machine is now capable of producing.

39.9%.  There was an overall increase in coil capacity of 166,500 Btuh, equating to the restoration of 13.9 tons 
of capacity or 32.2%.  There is also a reduction of 28.6% in both total power and watts per ton, which is 
another measurable way to view the thermodynamic enhancement of the PermaFrost NMR® ECM.  The 
result of the average ECM improvements is an ROI to Major Spice Manufacturer & Company of just 10.1 months based on 
the runtime information provided by the on-site senior mechanical technician.  The tables of data and 
financial calculations are available for review at the end of this report.

Product Brief
         PermaFrost NMR® is a multi-patented nanotechnology surface chemistry Energy Control Measure 
(ECM) that uses Nucleo Molecular Regenerative (NMR) technology as its core agent. A sustainable, 
one-time treatment with no down time required, PermaFrost NMR® lasts for the remaining life of any 
type of system in which it is installed – DX (direct expansion air and chilled water systems), Chillers 
(screw, reciprocating, scroll and centrifugal), heat pumps, ice making equipment.  Specialized 
applications include computer room cooling and dehumidification systems, chiller plants (water and ice 
production applications), domestic and industrial refrigeration (ammonia low and ultra low 
temperature), air-cooled single application water chillers and split and package rooftop HVAC 
equipment.
The direct benefits of PermaFrost NMR® are improved cooling performance, increased capacity and 
improved refrigerant velocity – all of which allows a system to achieve set point temperatures in a more 
rapid fashion which reduces system loading and operating periods.  The indirect benefits resulting from 
the enhanced thermodynamic characteristics following treatment include reduced run time, less kW 
hours used, less amp draw at the compressor, less metallic wear, longer overall equipment life and a 
reduced carbon footprint.

Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol
The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocols (IPMVP) are used to develop this 
report.  The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), American Society of Heating, Refrigeration and 
Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and The Efficiency Valuation Organization (EVO) accept the 
IPMVP as a global methodology for determining the effectiveness of energy conservation methods and 
products.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize.  They 
are options A, B, C and D.  Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report.  Option B is 
defined as: All parameter measurements with the boundary of the ECM (PermaFrost NMR®) as the single 
source of measurement.  Savings are determined by field measurement of the energy use of the ECM 
affected equipment or system and any performance enhancements versus the baseline data.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period.  For the boundary utilized for Option B short-term 
measurements are very useful as data when the variables are contained.  The savings are calculated by 
short-term measurements of baseline and reporting period energy, and /or engineering computations using 
measurements of proxies of energy use.

Energy Conservation Method (ECM) Content
The content within the following report will demonstrate the ability of PermaFrost NMR® to correct the 
effects of thermal degradation and fouling on the heat exchange surfaces.
 
A diagnostic examination of the pilot equipment was implemented to determine if the unit’s operational 
conditions were satisfactory.  Baseline measurements were recorded and then the proper amount and type 
of PermaFrost NMR™ was injected. The product was then allowed four (4) weeks to seat itself into the 
metal surfaces before post measurements were taken again to establish the efficiency gains. 
The following report produces the utilization of the IPMVP International Performance Measurement and 
Verification Protocol as the M&V plan.  The final calculations were performed by Powertron Global’s Senior 
Energy Engineer, [Senior Energy Engineer], ME/CEM/CMC/CMVP and witnessed by [Client Representative], Senior

Delta T = Return Air DB – Supply Air DB

Actual Btuh Capacity = Measured CFM * 4.5 * Enthalpy Delta (Baseline – Post)
 
System Eﬃciency % =  Actual Coil Capacity Btuh / Nominal Coil Capacity Btuh
 
EER = Btuh / Adjusted Watts

Conclusion
The IPMVP calculations and results for the referenced American Standard Split HVAC system model # 
TTA090 Condenser and the TWE090 air handler do not reflect the initial published design performance 
intent. This is indicative of many systems due to the variables that effect performance in-situ. 
The ARI Standards for determining the capacity of forced air coils AHRI-410-2001 sets standards for testing 
that qualify the printed statements of manufacturers. Equipment in-situ rarely matches these standard tests. 
Therefore although there are capacity levels within this report that do not coincide with published data 
from the respective manufacturer it is due to the following:
1. CFM is greater than the design intent.
2. Entering air for the evaporator coil is cooler than design intent.
3. Entering air for the condenser coil is cooler than the design intent.
All of the above in-situ conditions have altered the performance expected baseline and post analysis but 
since these conditions were repeated during the post analysis or avoided energy cost period the level of 
uncertainty is acceptable within the confines of the IPMVP.

Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol
The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP) was utilized in the 
development of this report. The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), The American Society of Heating, 
Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and The Efficiency Valuation Organization 
(EVO) accept the IPMVP as a global methodology for determining the effectiveness of energy conservation 
measures and products.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize. They 
are options A, B, C and D.  Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report. Option B is 
defined as: All parameter measurements with the boundary of the ECM as the single source of 
measurement. Savings are determined by field measurement of the energy use of the ECM affected 
equipment or system and any performance enhancements versus the baseline data.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period. For the boundary utilized for Option B short-term 
measurements are very useful as data when the variables are contained. The savings are calculated by 
short-term measurements of baseline and avoided energy reporting period (AERP), and /or engineering 
computations using measurements of proxies of energy use.

Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol
The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP) was utilized in the 
development of this report. The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), The American Society of Heating, 
Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and The Efficiency Valuation Organization 
(EVO) accept the IPMVP as a global methodology for determining the effectiveness of energy conservation 
methods and products.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize. They 
are options A, B, C and D.  Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report. Option B is 
defined as: All parameter measurements with the boundary of the ECM (PermaFrost NMR®) as the single 
source of measurement. Savings are determined by field measurement of the energy use of the ECM 
affected equipment or system and any performance enhancements versus the baseline data.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period.  For the boundary utilized for Option B short-term 
measurements are very useful as data when the variables are contained. The savings are calculated by 
short-term measurements of baseline and energy reporting period (post), and /or engineering computations 
using measurements of proxies of energy use.

2.0 OBJECTIVE

The objectives of the study were to verify the benefits afforded users of the PermaFrost product in
an ice machine application, in terms of reduction in energy consumption and the reduction of the
bin fill time. These benefits, in this application, can be translated into direct cost savings in the

production of ice in the hospitality industry.

3.0 DESCRIPTION OF SAMPLE

PermaFrost is a refrigerant additive reported to enhance the heat transfer. The client has indicated
that the product works by removing heat from metal surfaces, accelerating refrigerant flow,
increasing thermo-conductivity and heat transfer throughout the equipment. The client has
indicated that its unique molecular composition “passivates” and stabilizes the metal components
throughout the system, allowing for the refrigerant to absorb and dissipate heat at an accelerated

rate. In sealed systems, a single application is intended to last the life of the compressor.

5.0 Results

Test details - An ice cuber model Manitowoc GROISOA was tested before and after the
introduction of 1 oz of PermaFrost. This machine continuously circulates water over a cooled ice
trough. When the ice reaches a certain adjustable point it completes a circuit that triggers the
reverse hot cycle that heats the ice trough. The ice slides off the trough and into the bin. By doing
so the ice actuates a baffle connected to a switch that signals the compressor to resume the
cooling cycle. For this test the ice production time was measured and it was triggered off this
switch. The energy consumption was monitored on the incoming power supply to the entire unit.
Both prior to and after the introduction of PermaFrost the ice bin was completely empty so that

the cycle times were run under the same conditions.

The ice cycle time decreased from 20 minutes to 13 minutes, with a portion (approximately 2
minutes) of this being attributed to a cooler bin due to ice presence. A 25% reduction in ice
production time was attributed directly to the additive itself. The energy consumption decreased

by approximately 6% after the addition of Permafrost.

C. 
GENERAL FINDINGS 
1.
Method of Procedure for testing:
The objective of measuring the overall cooling production of HVAC systems can 
be realized by measuring the total energy consumed by the specific unit being 
tested and the total BTU production of the system then calculating these 
parameters to obtain kW per ton, EER (energy efficient ratio) and COP 
(coefficient of performance) Using that information the total BTUH of cooling 
production can be realized. The objective of measuring overall power consumed 
by an HVAC system can be realized by measuring voltage, amperage and power 
factor.  
For these specific HVAC systems many parameters were measured every two 
seconds for a period of seven (7) days for the development of a scientific 
baseline of performance and a post period of seven (7) days for the development 
of a scientific post analysis of performance. Data was extracted from the 
parameters measured every five (5) seconds during the normal operating hours 
of 9am to 5pm.  
Total BTUH was developed along with total kW consumption by measuring all 
required data points (13 points see appendix for points measured) and entering 
them into industry best practice engineering formulae. All measurement hardware 
was certified under NIST or CE standards. Engineering formulae was developed 
by AHRI / ASHRAE (American Heating and Refrigeration Institute / American 
Society of Heating Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Engineers) 
During regular business hours the outdoor air temperature entering the air-cooled 
condenser coils of each unit will affect the design capacity. Therefore we have 
provided baseline and post analysis of the seven (7) day periods at several 
outdoor air temperature intervals so as to provide the comparison of improved 
capacity and subsequent kW per ton, EER and COP across a variation of 
outdoor air temperatures consisting of a eleven (11) degree span (80-90 degrees 
F). 
D.  
CONCLUSION 
Testing validates that the PermaFrost NMR product does improve HVAC/R 
energy efficiency when added to the refrigerant circuit of a cooling system. 
ASHRAE estimates that air-conditioning will lose 30% of its cooling capacity due 
to the thermal degradation of internal surfaces. Higher percentages up to 40% 
have been observed in systems that have extremely high runtimes.

        This report contains specific information regarding the detailed forensic performance testing (outlined

Office Park A in [CITY REDACTED], NV.  The two 5-ton HVAC Equipment Manufacturer packaged rooftop units supporting the facility 
use R-22 refrigerant.  Both of the pilot units were installed in June of 2004 and are estimated to run 
approximately 3,050 hours per year. Immediately following the baseline testing, both units were treated 
with five ounces of the PermaFrost NMR® product specially formulated for R-22 DX systems.  
Since there were no other ECM’s going on during this pilot project, the improvement in efficiency and 
restored capacity gained directly at the units is solely attributable to the PermaFrost NMR® ECM.  The pilot 
units now provide colder and drier supply air and more Btu’s while using less power.  This greater 
operational efficiency is due to the restoration of the heat transfer ability of the evaporator and condenser 
coils, less metal to metal friction and improved refrigerant flow.  
Since the outside air temperatures and humidity were almost identical in the baseline and post reporting 
periods, as were the return air temperatures from inside the space, no adjustment for weather were made to 
the resulting numbers.
Following treatment with PermaFrost NMR® the two pilot units showed an average 22.7% reduction in 
Total Watts and a 14.7% reduction in Amps while at the same time producing an increase in capacity of 
11,340 Btuh or 11.1% more tonnage.  The units also showed a substantial reduction in Watts/Ton of 22.7% 
and an 11.1% improvement in the Enthalpy Delta.  Additionally, the two pilot units showed an average of 
29.7% improvement in EER, which is another measurable way to view the thermodynamic enhancement of 
the PermaFrost NMR® ECM.  The result of the average ECM improvements is an ROI to Real Estate Capital Firm A of just 
18.3 months. The tables of data and financial calculations are available for review at the end of this report.

         PermaFrost NMR® is a multi-patented nanotechnology surface chemistry Energy Control 
Measure (ECM) that uses Nucleo Molecular Regenerative (NMR) technology as its core agent.  A 
sustainable, one-time treatment with no down time required, PermaFrost NMR® lasts for the remaining 
life of any type of system in which it is installed – DX (direct expansion air and chilled water systems), 
Chillers (screw, reciprocating, scroll and centrifugal), heat pumps, ice making equipment.  Specialized 
applications include computer room cooling and dehumidification systems, chiller plants (water and 
ice production applications), domestic and industrial refrigeration (ammonia low and ultra low 
temperature), air-cooled single application water chillers and split and package rooftop HVAC 
equipment.
The direct benefits of PermaFrost NMR® are improved cooling performance, increased capacity and 
improved refrigerant velocity – all of which allows a system to achieve set point temperatures in a more 
rapid fashion which reduces system loading and operating periods.  The indirect benefits resulting 
from the enhanced thermodynamic characteristics following treatment include reduced run time, less 
kW hours used, less amp draw at the compressor, less metallic wear, longer overall equipment life and 
a reduced carbon footprint for Real Estate Capital Firm A.

Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol
The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocols (IPMVP) are used to develop this 
report.  The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), American Society of Heating, Refrigeration and 
Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and The Efficiency Valuation Organization (EVO) accept the 
IPMVP as a global methodology for determining the effectiveness of energy conservation methods and 
products.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize.  They 
are options A, B, C and D.  Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report.  Option B is 
defined as: All parameter measurements with the boundary of the ECM (PermaFrost NMR®) as the single 
source of measurement.  Savings are determined by field measurement of the energy use of the ECM 
affected equipment or system and any performance enhancements versus the baseline data.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period.  For the boundary utilized for Option B short-term 
measurements are very useful as data when the variables are contained.  The savings are calculated by 
short-term measurements of baseline and reporting period energy, and /or engineering computations using 
measurements of proxies of energy use.

HVAC/R Eﬃciency Report
Purpose of Energy Eﬃciency Study
The purpose of this study is to verify the industry wide problem of efficiency loss in HVAC/R as projected by 
ASHRAE research and to quantify the amount of money wasted due to this loss. Many industry leading 
organizations including ASHRAE project that all HVAC/R units degrade in capacity and efficiency as they age. 
Thermal degradation is caused by a phenomenon that is present in all HVACR equipment that operates as a 
vapor compression cycle associated with refrigerant and compressor lubricant. This thermal degradation is well 
documented by the HVACR industry and the original equipment manufacturers (OEM’s). Thermal degradation 
prevents units from operating at the original design efficiency, which leads to excessive run-times and additional 
kWh consumption.
The chiller in this study is representative of the portfolio of comfort cooling equipment operated by Gaming Company A 
Gaming throughout their [Gaming Company] Casino portfolio. If thermal degradation is present in this chiller, it is 
present in the entire inventory of equipment. Energy waste can be calculated based on this equipment (portfolio 
representation) and then accurately extrapolated across the entire inventory of equipment. 
Similarly, if the lost efficiency of this chiller can be 
restored, it would allow Major Gaming Company to keep it in 
service longer without sacrificing performance or 
energy consumption. It will also provide Gaming Company A 
Gaming and [Gaming Company] Casinos the flexibility of a 
much wider window of time wherein to undertake 
the costly capital expense of replacing it when it 
does finally reach the end of its useful life.

Detailed performance testing (outlined later in this report) was performed on the pilot chiller before and after 
the installation of the PermaFrost NMR® to determine the impact on the three key elements that greatly affect

Methodology
The measurements used in the efficiency calculations were collected and compiled in accordance with the 
IPMVP (International Measurement and Verification Protocol) framework. The team was led by Gaming Company A 
Gaming’s Facility Manager, [Client Representative] and [Client Representative], facilities technician. Also playing a key role in 
the pilot was Murphy Mechanical Services’ Jeff Gumm, Sr. Mechanical Engineer and [Senior Energy Engineer], 
Director of Engineering for Powertron Global.  The overall project was managed and directed by Joelle 
[Personnel Name], Asst. General Manager for [Gaming Venue REDACTED].  
Engineering Notes 
Both the baseline and post readings were taken at 90% load with incoming condenser water at 84 degrees and incoming 
chilled water at 55 degrees, therefore no adjustments were made to the resulting data. Major Gaming Company’s management of the 
chiller plant combined with the building load during the trial provided more than an adequate heat load on the facility to 
ensure the chiller would remain running during the actual data collection period.  
The chiller was tested over the span of nearly three months. During the trial the chiller experienced an unrelated oil seal 
failure and loss of some oil & refrigerant. Oil samples from the chiller at the time of the seal failure revealed the oil was still 
serviceable with no abnormalities present. Since PermaFrost NMR® had already had time to seat into the metal surfaces of 
the heat exchanges, the chiller did not need to be retreated. Once put back into operation, the chiller was allowed to run for 
an additional week before post readings were taken.
The boundary of the testing was the chiller and nothing else, therefore confidence in the accuracy of the performance 
calculations is very high.

Energy Conservation Method (ECM)
The content detailed in this report will first demonstrate the ability of the pilot chiller to perform prior to the 
PermaFrost NMR® (ECM) being installed, as well as illustrate the amount of thermal degradation due in large 
part to thermal degradation within the heat exchangers (evaporator and condenser barrels).  The following report 
produces the utilization of the IPMVP as the M&V plan. 
The results were formulated by entering the data into the following applicable thermodynamic 
engineering formulas:
 
• kW = Volts * Amps * Power Factor of 1.47/1000 (for 3-Phase) 
 
• kW/Ton = kW / Actual Tonnage 
 
• Coefficient of Performance (COP) = (12 / kW per ton /3.412)
 
• Actual Cooling Tons per Hour = Evaporator GPM X 8.34 * 60 * Chilled Water Delta T / 12,000 BTU 
 
• Refrigerant Approach = Supply Water Temp – Saturated Evaporator Temp (CH)

Utilizing data in the charts on the previous pages, to obtain a true avoided energy cost and subsequent payback period for 
Major Gaming Company for implementing the PermaFrost NMR®, a detailed Regression Analysis is used to calculate the true 
energy savings resulting from the improvement in capacity. This increased capacity reduces the annual kWh expended in 
the Post Analysis Period or reduces the load. ROI comes from determining what the cost to run the systems was when 
operating at the original energy profile to produce the newly restored amount of available tonnage capacity and then 
subtracting the revised cost to run the systems at the same restored tonnage after the PermaFrostNMR® was installed.

building set points with increased efficiency resulting in reduced compressor demand loading.

Methodology
The measurements used in the efficiency calculations were collected and compiled in accordance with the 
IPMVP (International Measurement and Verification Protocol) framework. NIST calibrated devices where 
used for the highest level of accuracy and data integrity. IPMVP is the industry standard according to the 
US Department of Energy. Because of its wide international adoption, the IPMVP has been identified as the 
best Measurement and Verification Framework for helping to determine and secure financial compensation 
for emissions reductions resulting from Energy Conservation Methods (ECM).
Measurement and Verification (M&V) was conducted to establish an initial energy baseline and a post avoided 
energy-reporting period. The purpose of the testing was to show how the ECM improves the thermal 
performance of any system it is installed in.
The improvement in efficiency and restored capacity gained directly at each unit was solely attributable to 
PermaFrost NMR®. This is a result of the reversal of thermal inefficiency on the heat exchanger surfaces.

Energy Conservation Method (ECM)
The content within the following report will demonstrate the ability of PermaFrost NMR® to correct the 
effects of thermal degradation and fouling on the heat exchange surfaces. 
 
A diagnostic examination of the pilot equipment was implemented to determine if the operational conditions 
of the systems were satisfactory. Baseline M&V was recorded on the unit and then the proper amount and type 
of PermaFrost NMR® was injected directly into the suction side of the refrigerant loop. The gestation period 
for the pilot was approximately 4 weeks. At the end of this gestation period, Post M&V results were taken in 
the identical manner as in the baseline, taking special care to match the same outside air temperatures 
however the entering condenser water was warmer by 5.04% in the Energy Reporting Period (Post). No 
weather adjustments in the Post were taken due to this increase in incoming condenser water.
The results were formulated by entering the data into the following thermodynamic engineering formulas:
• kW = Volts * Amps * Power Factor of 1.47/1000 (for 3-Phase) 
• kW/Ton = kW / Actual Tonnage 
• Coefficient of Performance (COP) = (12 / kW per ton /3.412)
• Actual Cooling Tons per Hour = Evaporator GPM X 8.34 * 60 * Chilled Water Delta T / 12,000 BTU 
• Refrigerant Approach = Supply Water Temp – Saturated Evaporator Temp (CH) or Supply Air  - Saturated 
  Evaporator Temp (DX)

Executive Summary
        This report contains specific information regarding the installation of the energy control measure 
(ECM) PermaFrost NMR® for Major Golf Organization HQ located in Ponte Verde, FL. Detailed forensic performance 
testing (outlined later in this report) was performed on 2 split system DX units. 
Immediately following the baseline testing, the units were treated with the proper amount and type of 
PermaFrost NMR® product formulated for R-22 DX systems. Since there were no other ECM’s going on 
during this pilot project, the improvement in efficiency and restored capacity gained directly at the units is 
solely attributable to the PermaFrost NMR® ECM. The units now provide cooler/drier supply air while 
using less power. This greater operational efficiency is due to the restoration of the heat transfer ability of 
the evaporator and condenser coils.
Following treatment with the PermaFrost NMR® technology, the 2 units showed an average 35.9% 
reduction in kW/ton based on the exact capacity measured in the baseline M&V and the post gestation 
M&V. The units showed an average 50.9% reduction in kWh. Prior to the ECM, the units produced a total of 
4.64 tons of cooling. After the ECM, the tonnage produced increased to 6.09 tons. This capacity increase 
from the baseline performance level led to an effective net average increase in COP of 71.5%. All of these 
factors directly correlate to what Major Golf Organization HQ building will realize in energy savings as they operate these 
units in the future under the same parameters.
The result of the ECM improvements is a ROI to the customer of a matter of months. The tables of data and 
financial calculations are available for review at the end of this report.

Product Brief
         PermaFrost NMR® is a multi-patented nanotechnology surface chemistry Energy Control Measure 
(ECM) that uses Nucleo Molecular Regenerative® (NMR™) technology as its core agent. A sustainable, 
one-time treatment with no down time required, PermaFrost NMR® lasts for the remaining life of any type 
of system in which it is installed. Examples of the types of commercial HVAC/R systems and equipment 
that PermaFrost NMR® has proven success with are direct expansion air systems (DX); chilled water 
systems (both flooded and DX; air and water cooled); ice making equipment; ammonia refrigeration plants 
(single compressor and cascade) and variable refrigerant flow (VRF) designs. The equipment utilized in 
these systems within our expanding portfolio of clients includes centrifugal (single and multi-stage), scroll, 
reciprocating and screw configurations.
The direct benefits of PermaFrost NMR® are improved cooling performance, increased capacity and 
improved refrigerant velocity – all of which allow systems to achieve set point temperatures in a more 
rapid fashion which reduces compressor operating periods. The indirect benefits resulting from the 
enhanced thermodynamic characteristics following treatment include reduced run time, less kW hours 
used, less amp draw at the compressor, longer equipment life cycle time and a reduced carbon footprint for 
the Major Golf Organization HQ.

Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol
The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP) is utilized in the 
development of this report. The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), American Society of Heating, 
Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and The Efficiency Valuation Organization 
(EVO) accept the IPMVP as a global methodology for determining the effectiveness of energy conservation 
methods and products.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize. They 
are options A, B, C and D.  Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report. Retrofit Isolation 
(Option B) is defined as: All parameter measurement with the boundary of the ECM (PermaFrost NMR®) as 
the single source of measurement. Savings are determined by field measurement of the energy use of the 
energy conservation method affected equipment or system and any performance enhancements versus the 
baseline data.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period.  For the boundary utilized for Option B short-term 
measurements are very useful as data when the variables are contained. The savings are calculated by 
short-term measurements of baseline and reporting period energy, and /or engineering computations using 
measurements of proxies of energy use.
