Energy Conservation Method (ECM) Content
The content of the following report will demonstrate the effects of PermaFrost NMR®’s ability to correct the 
effects of thermal degradation and fouling on the heat exchange surfaces. 
It was determined with Major Golf Organization HQ to treat two small split system DX units. A diagnostic examination of 
the pilot equipment is implemented to determine if the unit’s operational conditions are satisfactory. 
Baseline measurements will be recorded and then the proper amount and type of PermaFrost NMR® will be 
injected. The product will be allowed 4 weeks to seat itself into the metal surfaces. At the end of this 
gestation period, Post M&V results were taken in the identical manner as in the baseline, taking special care 
to match the same or very similar entering air temperatures and compressor discharge pressures. These are 
the two most critical measurements affected by the weather. Some units in this report required 
normalization due to weather.
It was determined with Steve Cantrell of the Major Golf Organization HQ that the units run approximately 3,000 hours 
annually at a kWh cost of .1204 cents per kW. 
The following report produces the utilization of the IPMVP International Performance Measurement and 
Verification Protocol as the M&V plan. Powertron Global’s Forensic Mechanical Engineer, Edward R. 
[Senior Energy Engineer], performed the final calculations and measurements.

the PermaFrost NMR® ECM, a detailed Regression Analysis is used to account for the amount of tonnage restored to

HVAC/R Eﬃciency Report
Purpose of the Study
This comprehensive efficiency study was conducted in an effort to verify the effectiveness of the PermaFrost 
NMR®  Energy Conservation Measure (ECM) in two large, mission critical centrifugal chillers located on 
opposite sides of the country. The chiller selected represent and to document the future avoided energy costs 
associated with the same. The chillers selected represent a microcosm of the overall Data Center Provider portfolio of chiller 
equipment. This allows the average savings percentage achieved and the future avoided energy costs calculated 
to be easily extrapolated out five and 10 years into the future to determine the viability of the business case.  
Understanding the Opportunity for Efficiency Restoration
All Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration (HVACR) systems experience thermal
degradation over time. Internal surfaces of heat exchangers lose their optimal thermal transfer
characteristics, resulting in reduced capacity, lower efficiency, and higher operating costs. This
degradation affects superheat levels and overall system performance, impacting the useful
equipment life of the HVACR system.
Restoring System Efficiency with PermaFrost NMR
PermaFrost NMR® technology addresses this thermal degradation by creating a permanent thermal
metal coating on the tube walls, whether on the inside or outside surfaces depending on the HVACR
equipment. This coating conditions the metal surfaces, reducing friction and restoring the system's
original thermal transfer efficiency. In every application this results in a lower per unit cost of cooling
which ultimately translates into lower overall energy costs.

Methodology
Detailed performance testing (outlined later in this report) was performed on the pilot Chillers before and 
after the installation of the ECM to determine the impact on the three key elements as they relate to the 
original design specifications that greatly affect the power bills:
 
 
1. The cooling capacity the Chillers are capable of producing after 6+ years in service. 
 
2. The actual cost of power required to produce the amount of cooling tons the Chillers are delivering 
 
    as reflected in the kW/ton measurement. 
 
3. The thermal dynamic ability of the Chillers to still perform at or close to operational design.
The measurements used in the efficiency calculations were collected and compiled in accordance with the 
IPMVP (International Measurement and Verification Protocol) testing framework. 
Due to operational constraints relating to ongoing construction schedules in the chiller plant, the testing at 
[Southeast Location] Metro was started on 20 November 2013 and concluded on 4 December 2013. This gave the ECM just 
over 330 hours to gestate within the chiller and improve thermal performance. The ECM normally produces 
90% or more of the improvement benefits it will ultimately deliver at 400+ runtime hours.
The testing at [Facility REDACTED] was started on 23 January 2014 and concluded on 26 February 2014. This allowed 
the ECM just over 600 hours to gestate within the chiller and improve thermal performance.
Notes
The boundary of the testing was the Chillers themselves, flange to flange while matching the baseline and post water 
temperatures entering the condenser and the returning chilled water temperatures entering the evaporator; therefore 
confidence in the accuracy of the performance calculations is very high. Very similar flow rates were used in both testing 
periods.

Product Brief

(ECM) that uses Nucleo Molecular Regenerative (NMR) technology as its core agent. A sustainable, 
one-time treatment with no down time required, PermaFrost NMR® lasts for the remaining life of any 
type of system in which it is installed. Examples of the types of commercial HVACR systems and 
equipment that PermaFrost NMR® has proven success with are direct expansion air systems (DX); 
chilled water systems (both flooded and DX; air and water cooled); ice making equipment; ammonia 
refrigeration plants (single compressor and cascade) and variable refrigerant flow (VRF) designs. The 
equipment utilized in these systems within our expanding portfolio of clients includes centrifugal (single 
and multi-stage), scroll, reciprocating and screw configurations.
The direct benefits of PermaFrost NMR® are improved cooling performance, increased capacity and 
improved refrigerant velocity – all of which allow systems to achieve set point temperatures in a more 
rapid fashion which reduces compressor operating periods. The indirect benefits resulting from the 
enhanced thermodynamic characteristics following treatment include reduced run time, less kW hours 
used, less amp draw at the compressor, longer equipment life cycle time and a reduced carbon footprint 
for Data Center Provider.

Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol
The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP) was utilized in the 
development of this report. The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), The American Society of Heating, 
Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and The Efficiency Valuation Organization 
(EVO) accept the IPMVP as a global methodology for determining the effectiveness of energy conservation 
methods and products.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize. They 
are options A, B, C and D.  Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report. Option B is 
defined as: All parameter measurements with the boundary of the ECM (PermaFrost NMR®) as the single 
source of measurement. Savings are determined by field measurement of the energy use of the ECM 
affected equipment or system and any performance enhancements versus the baseline data.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period. For the boundary utilized for Option B short-term 
measurements are very useful as data when the variables are contained. The savings are calculated by 
short-term measurements of baseline and energy reporting period (post), and /or engineering computations 
using measurements of proxies of energy use.

Verification Protocol (IPMVP) as the M&V plan. Charles Tedesco, Monsen Engineering, a Test and Balance

HVAC/R Eﬃciency Report
Purpose of Energy Eﬃciency Study
The purpose of this study is to verify that the restored capacity produced two years ago when all four rooftop 
units (RTU’s) were first treated with the PermaFrost NMR® is being sustained.  This same efficiency 
improvement is then quantified into dollars saved by National Restaurant Chain in the treated RTU’s. 
The roof top units involved in this study are representative of a great majority of the portfolio of equipment 
operated by National Restaurant Chain. The same information gathered in the study is then extrapolated out across the 
entire National Restaurant Chain portfolio to closely estimate what capacity has already been lost in term of increased 
energy costs. This same extrapolation methodology is also used to estimate what the potential future avoided 
wasted energy costs are expected to be when treating all RTU’s, refrigeration and ice machines.  
Many industry leading organizations, including the American Society of Heating, Refrigeration and Air 
Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), project that all heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration 
(HVACR) units degrade in capacity and efficiency as they operate and age. Thermal degradation is caused by a 
phenomenon that is present in all HVACR equipment that operates as a vapor compression cycle associated 
with refrigerant and compressor lubricant. This thermal degradation is well documented by the HVACR industry 
and the original equipment manufacturers (OEM’s). Thermal degradation prevents units from operating at the 
original design efficiency, which leads to excessive run-times and additional kWh consumption.

Process
This report contains specific information regarding the current performance profile of four similar RTU’s treated 
two years ago with PermaFrost NMR® compared to where ASHRAE degradation averages had them performing 
prior to treatment. A fifth similar RTU that was installed on the roof of one of the same four restaurants six 
months following initial equipment PermaFrost NMR® treatment (which was not treated) serves as a control unit 
and as another valuable way to demonstrate the value gained through the use of PermaFrost NMR®. 
Detailed performance testing (outlined later in this report) was performed on the pilot RTU’s unit after the 
installation of PermaFrost NMR® to determine the impact on the three key elements that greatly affect the restaurant chain 
Tuesday’s power bill as they relate to the original design specifications: 
 
1.  The cooling capacity the RTU’s are capable of producing after an average of 11 years in service.
 
2.  The actual cost of power required to produce the amount of cooling tons the RTU’s are delivering as 
      
     reflected in the kW/ton measurement. 
 
3.  The thermal dynamic ability of the RTU’s to continue to perform at or close to operational design.
Methodology
The measurements used in the efficiency calculations were collected and compiled in accordance with the 
IPMVP (International Measurement and Verification Protocol) framework. The team consisted of 
Energy Consulting Partner's CEO, [CEO] and Powertron Global’s Director of Engineering, [Senior Energy Engineer].  The 
manager on duty at each of the locations signed off on all the measurements taken prior to the team leaving 
each location, preserving the integrity of the data.
Notes 
Since power bills for the four restaurants already show savings, the focus of the field M&V was on determining the current 
performance levels of the four pilot RTU’s. The RTU’s were also compared to historical performance characteristics of 
themselves two years earlier and to a newer similar RTU that was not treated with the ECM. This helps to closely estimate 
the amount of savings already achieved by National Restaurant Chain and helps determine the impact of future savings.  
The readings were taken in the same conditions used by Air-Conditioning, Heating, & Refrigeration Institute (AHRI) to 
issue capacity ratings. All RTU’s were tested in sunny conditions with outside air temperatures between 80-82 degrees. 
The boundary of the testing was the RTU’s and nothing else; therefore confidence in the accuracy of the performance 
calculations is very high.

Energy Conservation Method (ECM)
The content detailed in this report will first demonstrate the ability of the pilot RTU’s to perform prior to and 
following the ECM being installed. The report will also illustrate the amount of thermal degradation that had 
occurred due in large part to thermal degradation within the heat exchangers and how much of that has been 
restored.
 
The following report produces the utilization of the IPMVP as the M&V plan. 
The results were formulated by entering the data into the following thermodynamic engineering formulas:
 
• kW = Volts * Amps * Power Factor of 1.47/1000 (for 3-Phase) 
 
• Tons = (Airflow * 4.5 * Enthalpy Delta) / 12,000 
 
• KW/Ton = kW / Actual Tonnage 
 
• Coefficient of Performance (COP) = (12 / kW per ton /3.412)
 
• Refrigerant Approach = Supply Air Temp – Saturated Suction Temp 
Notes 
Following a diagnostic examination of the pilot equipment to determine the operational condition of the system was still 
satisfactory; two-year post ECM data was collected and recorded by the M&V team. The delta of these measurements and 
associated historical baseline performance calculations show the amount of capacity restored and amount of money saved.
The following IPMVP data points were recorded on 25 & 26 May 2014 using recently purchased devices calibrated in 
accordance with NIST (National Institutes of Standards and Technology) standards to insure measurement accuracy. 
The RTU’s were initially treated with the ECM in March 2012. The two years since then not only ensures the ECM had 
ample time to prove longevity of the thermal benefits. All measurements were taken at 100% load and at similar return 
air and outdoor air temperatures.

Summary of HVAC/R Eﬃciency Study Results
RTU Unit Eﬃciency with PermaFrost NMR® ECM
National Restaurant Chain is experiencing significant thermal degradation in its HVAC/R units. The lower baseline 
operating tonnage and COP ratings are calculated based on historical data and are in line with the ASHRAE 
loss of performance and cost to operate numbers. The degraded equipment performance was costing the restaurant chain 
Tuesday significant money and wasting energy in the four pilot RTU’s. The equipment was using significantly 
more kWh to operate than they did when they were new.
The performance summary includes the measured efficiency and tonnage of the RTU’s in the baseline and post 
testing periods demonstrating the impact of thermal degradation. The implementation of PermaFrost NMR® 
ECM in the four RTU’s averaging 11 years of age resulted in a restoration of 10.42 operating tons and an 
average improvement of 31.6% in Coefficient of Performance (COP), significantly reducing the cost to operate 
the RTU’s throughout the year.
When compared to the newer untreated control RTU, the pilot RTU’s are already outperforming it. The 11 year 
old units are averaging 9.82 tons of cooling produced while the Control Unit has already slipped to 9.37 tons. 
This difference of .45 tons means the older units are producing an average of 4.8% more tonnage than the 
Control Unit and a corresponding improvement in COP of 6.35%.

Utilizing data in the charts on the previous pages, to obtain a true avoided energy cost and subsequent payback period 
for National Restaurant Chain for implementing the PermaFrost NMR®, a detailed Regression Analysis is used to calculate the true 
energy savings resulting from the improvement in capacity. This increased capacity reduces the annual kWh expended 
in the Post Analysis Period. ROI comes from determining what the cost to run the systems was when operating at the 
original energy profile to produce the newly restored amount of available tonnage capacity and then subtracting the 
revised cost to run the systems at the same restored tonnage after the PermaFrostNMR® was installed. This regression 
analysis is the most widely accepted method of accounting for the reduced number of hours the systems will now operate 
due to the restored capacity. This restored capacity allows the systems to reach the internal building set points with 
increased efficiency resulting in reduced compressor demand loading.

one-time treatment with no down time required, PermaFrost NMR® lasts for the remaining life of any 
type of system in which it is installed – DX (direct expansion air and chilled water systems), Chillers 
(screw, reciprocating, scroll and centrifugal), heat pumps, ice making equipment.  Specialized 
applications include computer room cooling and dehumidification systems, chiller plants (water and ice 
production applications), domestic and industrial refrigeration (ammonia low and ultra low 
temperature), air-cooled single application water chillers and split and package rooftop HVAC 
equipment.
The direct benefits of PermaFrost NMR® are improved cooling performance, increased capacity, and 
improved refrigerant velocity – all of which allows a system to achieve set point temperatures in a more 
rapid fashion that reduces system loading and operating periods.  The indirect benefits resulting from 
the enhanced thermodynamic characteristics following treatment include reduced run time, less kW 
hours used, less amp draw at the compressor, less metallic wear and longer overall equipment life.

Executive Summary
This report contains specific information regarding the installation of PermaFrost NMR® in the 20-ton 
Comfort-Aire DX HVAC unit at Organization A, 2nd floor, [Commercial Address], NY.  The unit is owned 
and maintained by Organization A (heretofore referred to as The Company) located in New York, NY. 
[Client Representative], P.E. representing Organization A, oversaw the trial. 
The improved/restored efficiency on the unit directly attributable to the PermaFrost NMR® ECM was 
substantial.  The unit now provides cooler supply air with greater efficiency due to the restoration of the 
heat transfer capacity of the evaporator and condenser coils and increased the available useful tonnage. 
Please note that this system is subjected to excessive discharge refrigerant temperatures and subsequent 
pressures.  These issues at times cause nuisance tripping of the discharge pressure safety switch that then 
causes the unit to shut down.  During the initial baseline data recording period this condition was observed 
and as a result the pressure drop across the condenser coil was measured.  This pressure difference should 
not exceed 0.50".  The measured pressure drop measured during this baseline reporting period was in excess 
of 2".
 
It was also our understanding that the condenser coil was cleaned by a service group to attempt to alleviate 
this condition.  The post energy measurement period revealed that the discharge pressure is  in excess of 305 
psi.  This necessitated another measurement of the pressure drop across the condenser coil and this revealed 
that the pressure drop is continuing to measure in excess of 2".  The method of cleaning to this coil has not 
produced the required relief for the system to completely condense all of the discharge gas.  We suggest that 
this condenser coil be cleaned with the proper chemicals and water as the manufacturer instructs.  When 
this pressure is reduced, the savings as a result of the installation of PermaFrost NMR® will be even greater.
The overall system efficiency improved by 12.7% and the EER improved by 12.4%.  There was an increase in 
coil capacity of 19,969 in Btuh which equates to gaining 1.7-tons of capacity or 12.5%.  There is also a 
reduction of 10.9% in total power and watts per ton which is another measurable way to view the 
thermodynamic enhancement of the PermaFrost NMR® ECM.  The tables of data and financial calculations 
are available for review at the end of this report.  The result of these combined ECM improvements is an 
ROI to The Company of 27.2 months.

Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol
The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocols (IPMVP) are used to develop this 
report. The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), American Society of Heating, Refrigeration and 
Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and The Efficiency Valuation Organization (EVO) accept the 
IPMVP as a global methodology for determining the effectiveness of energy conservation methods and 
products.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize.  They 
are options A, B, C and D.  Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report.  Option B is 
defined as: All parameter measurements with the boundary of the ECM (Permafrost NMR®) as the single 
source of measurement.  Savings are determined by field measurement of the energy use of the ECM 
affected equipment or system and any performance enhancements versus the baseline data.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period.  For the boundary utilized for Option B short-term 
measurements are very useful as data when the variables are contained. The savings are calculated by 
short-term measurements of baseline and reporting period energy, and /or engineering computations using 
measurements of proxies of energy use. 
The final computation follows the formula:
Option B savings = Baseline Energy – Reporting Period Energy
+ - Routine adjustments + - Non-Routine Adjustments

Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol
The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP) was utilized in the 
development of this report. The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), The American Society of Heating, 
Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and The Efficiency Valuation Organization 
(EVO) accept the IPMVP as a global methodology for determining the effectiveness of energy conservation 
methods and products.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize. They 
are options A, B, C and D.  Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report. Option B is 
defined as: All parameter measurements with the boundary of the ECM as the single source of 
measurement. Savings are determined by field measurement of the energy use of the ECM affected 
equipment or system and any performance enhancements versus the baseline data.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period.  For the boundary utilized for Option B short-term 
measurements are very useful as data when the variables are contained. The savings are calculated by 
short-term measurements of baseline and energy reporting period (post), and /or engineering computations 
using measurements of proxies of energy use.

Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol
The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP) was utilized in the 
development of this report. The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), The American Society of Heating, 
Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and The Efficiency Valuation Organization 
(EVO) accept the IPMVP as a global methodology for determining the effectiveness of energy conservation 
methods and products.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize. They 
are options A, B, C and D.  Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report. Option B is 
defined as: All parameter measurements with the boundary of the ECM as the single source of 
measurement. Savings are determined by field measurement of the energy use of the ECM affected 
equipment or system and any performance enhancements versus the baseline data.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period.  For the boundary utilized for Option B short-term 
measurements are very useful as data when the variables are contained. The savings are calculated by 
short-term measurements of baseline and energy reporting period (post), and /or engineering computations 
using measurements of proxies of energy use.

Methodology
After verifying the amount of air flowing across the evaporator coils before beginning each pilot, the 
subsequent measurements used in the efficiency calculations were collected using AHRI Standards 210/240
& 340/360 and compiled in accordance with Option B of the IPMVP (International Measurement and 
Verification Protocol) framework.   
The results presented below were formulated by entering the data into the following thermodynamic 
engineering formulas:
 
• kW = Volts * Amps * Power Factor of 1.47/1000 (for 3-Phase) 
 
• kW/ton = Actual Measured Energy / Actual Measured Capacity 
 
• Coefficient of Performance (COP) = 12 / (kW/ton) /3.412
 
• Actual Cooling Capacity per Hour = (Measured CFM * 4.5 * Enthalpy Delta T) / 12,000 BTU

Explanation of Regression Analysis
Utilizing data collected during the pilot study, to obtain a true avoided energy cost and subsequent payback period for TD 
Bank for implementing the PermaFrost NMR® ECM, a detailed Regression Analysis is used to calculate the true energy 
savings resulting from the improvement in both capacity and efficiency. Working together, these improvements reduce the 
annual kWh expended in the Post Analysis Period. The ROI comes from determining what the cost to run the cooling systems 
was when operating at the original energy profile to produce the newly restored amount of available capacity and then 
subtracting the revised cost to run the systems at the same restored capacity after the PermaFrostNMR® ECM was installed. 
This regression analysis is the most widely accepted method of accounting for the reduced number of hours and/or load % at 
which the systems will now operate due to the restored performance profile. This restored performance profile allows the 
cooling systems to satisfy the internal area set point with increased efficiency resulting in reduced compressor demand loading.

Purpose of Energy Eﬃciency Study
Thermal degradation is well documented by the American Society of Heating, Refrigeration and Air 
Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE) and the original equipment manufacturers (OEM’s). It is a major cause of 
capacity loss in Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration (HVACR) systems, preventing them 
from operating at the original design efficiency soon after initial installation in the field. 
The purpose of this study is to verify the effectiveness of the PermaFrost NMR® Energy Conservation Measure 
(ECM) in a water-cooled package unit at the Beverage Company/Beverage Company Beverage Company B Factory and document the future avoided 
energy costs associated with the same.

Process
This comprehensive report contains specific information regarding the performance profile of a single water 
cooled packaged unit (PU) that supports the Beverage Company B Factory. The detailed performance testing (outlined 
later in this report) was performed on the PU before (baseline) and after (post) the installation of PermaFrost 
NMR®. 
This testing determined the impact on three key elements relating to the original design specifications that 
greatly affect the HVAC portion of the Beverage Company B Factory power bill. They include:
 
1. The cooling capacity the PU is capable of producing after just seven (7) years in service. 
 
2. The actual cost of power required to produce the amount of cooling tons the PU is delivering as  
 
reflected in the kW/ton measurement. 
 
3. The thermal dynamic ability of the equipment to still perform at or close to operational design.  
Methodology
The measurements used in the efficiency calculations were collected and compiled in accordance with the 
IPMVP (International Measurement and Verification Protocol) framework.
 
[Client Director of Engineering] of Beverage Company and [Client Mechanical Engineer] of HVAC Contractor B witnessed and verified the recording of all of the 
pilot measurements while being observed by Powertron Global’s Director of Engineering, [Senior Energy Engineer].
  
The baseline day chosen to test the PU’s was an average day temperature and humidity-wise for the [South African Location] 
area in the fall and winter which ensured repeatability of similar weather for the post testing measurements.  
The weather and factory conditions on both days provided an adequate heat load on the facility to ensure both 
compressors in the system would remain running during the actual data collection period. The boundary of 
the testing was the PU and nothing else; therefore confidence in the accuracy of the performance calculations 
is very high.

Energy Conservation Method (ECM)
The content detailed in the first phase of this report will first demonstrate the ability of the pilot PU to perform 
prior to the ECM being installed, as well as illustrate the amount of thermal degradation due in large part to 
thermal degradation within the heat exchangers. 
Following a diagnostic examination of the pilot equipment to determine the operational condition of the 
system was satisfactory, Baseline M&V data was collected and recorded by the M&V team. Approximately 3 
months after installation of PermaFrost NMR®, the M&V team returned on a very similar weather day to the 
Baseline to take Post M&V measurements in the identical fashion as in the Baseline. The delta of these 
measurements and associated calculations show the amount of capacity restored.
The following report produces the utilization of the IPMVP as the M&V plan. 
The results were formulated by entering the data into the following thermodynamic engineering formulas:
 
• kW = Volts * Amps * Power Factor of 1.47/1000 (for 3-Phase) 
 
• Ton = (Airflow * 4.5 * Enthalpy Delta) / 12,000 
 
• kW/Ton = kW / Actual Tonnage 
 
• Coefficient of Performance (COP) = (12 / kW per ton /3.412)

HVAC/R Eﬃciency Study Results
Calculated Eﬃciency of Tea Factory HVAC PU Baseline and Post
The measurements taken show just how far off design the Tea Factory pilot PU (#79) had degraded in terms 
of efficiency over seven (7) years of use. This same pilot PU was determined to be performing at an average of 
43% of the original design efficiency in the baseline. The actual design rated tonnage of the PU is 20 tons. In 
actuality, the PU was only producing a total of 8.4 tons of cooling at the start of the pilot. Approximately half of 
this 57% efficiency loss is directly attributable to the thermal degradation of the heat exchange surfaces over a 
short period of time. This is due in large part to thermal degradation which creates an insulating barrier to heat 
transfer on the tube walls (inside the tube on a Direct Expansion system and outside the tube on a flooded 
evaporator chiller). The remaining efficiency loss is a result of the reduced inlet and outlet air ducting 
configuration used in conjunction with this and all the other PU’s in the factory. The actual airflow across the 
coil in the PU is only about 50% of design so the focus of this in-situ pilot will be on the improvement delta 
over the baseline rather than against design.
After the ECM was installed, the average efficiency in the PU increased to 54% of design specifications, 
equating to 10.8 total tons. The restoration of 2.4 tons represents a 28.6% increase in capacity.

develop this report. The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), American Society of Heating, Refrigeration

products.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize.  They 
are options A, B, C and D.  Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report.  Option B is 
defined as: All parameter measurements with the boundary of the ECM (PermaFrost NMR®) as the single 
source of measurement within the equipment that was affected.
Savings are determined by field measurement of the energy use of the ECM affected equipment or system 
and any performance enhancements versus the baseline data prior to the ECM.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period.  For the boundary utilized for Option B, short-term 
measurements are very useful as data when the variables are contained.  The savings are calculated by 
short-term measurements of baseline and reporting period energy, and /or engineering computations using 
measurements of proxies of energy use.

Conclusion
The resulting improvements in the performance efficiency of the chiller generated by the ECM are deemed 
to be substantial.  Prior to the introduction of PermaFrost NMR®, this chiller was introduced to a full load 
test.  This test determined the operational characteristics of the chiller’s ability to reach full load of design 
and performance.  The test also recorded the machine’s energy consumption while sustained at that load 
without load variance.  The outdoor air temperature during the baseline-testing period was 77 degrees and 
the set point of the chiller was adjusted to 43 degrees.  Chiller load was attributable to directing the energy 
management system to command all chilled water valves in the air handler directory to the 100% open 
position for the duration of this data gathering exercise. 
The machine loaded the compressor to 100% load while consuming 430 amps of electrical energy.  Note that 
this chiller was unable to attain the desired chilled water set point of 43 degrees during the baseline 
energy-testing period as full load limits were reached before the chilled water set point was achieved.  Also 
note that due to the energy load on the compressor, this machine was limited to the development of 381 
tons during this phase of the baseline test.
After the baseline testing, data was cataloged and PermaFrost NMR® was introduced into the suction and 
condensed liquid refrigerant inlet service ports.  This machine was then operated for a period of 28 days to 
provide the gestation period necessary for PermaFrost NMR® to absorb into all heat exchange surfaces.
Subsequent to the baseline test period for determining chiller performance and energy consumption, a 
replication of conditions were developed to determine the avoided cost of performance and operating levels 
(post testing period).  The outdoor temperature during this post-test was slightly warmer at 79 degrees and 
the set point was again adjusted to 43 degrees.  Once again, chiller load was attributable to directing the 
energy management system to command all chilled water valves in the air handler directory to the 100% 
open position for the duration of the post or (avoided energy) data gathering period of this exercise (or test). 
This is the identical load profile used for the baseline-testing period of the ECM.  Note that load was slightly 
greater than the baseline-reporting period due to the outdoor air temperature being higher.  No adjustments 
were made in the baseline reading to reflect this increase in outdoor air temperature so as to reflect 
confidence in the energy savings produced.

Executive Summary
This report contains specific information regarding the installation of PermaFrost NMR® in Unit #2 of two
16-ton Liebert Computer Room Air Conditioning (CRAC) supporting mission critical data center operations 
for this U.S. Communications Company (heretofore referred to as The Company) located in Long Island, 
New York.
Two Company representatives, one from Network Engineering and the other from Power and Energy 
Planning section of the Global Real Estate Department, managed this entire trial.  They were supported by 
The Company’s on-site contractor engineering support personnel.
The improved/restored efficiency on Unit #2 directly attributable to the PermaFrost NMR® ECM was 
substantial.  Unit #2 now provides cooler supply air with greater efficiency due to the restoration of the heat 
transfer capacity of the evaporator and condenser coils and increased the available useful tonnage. 
The overall efficiency improved by 27.5% and the EER improved by 35.4%.  There was an increase in coil 
capacity of 52,812 in Btuh which equates to gaining more than 4-tons of capacity or 32.1%.  There is also an 
improvement of 5.4 degrees F in Delta T (difference between supply and return air) which is another 
measurable way to view the thermodynamic enhancement of the PermaFrost NMR® ECM. 
The tables of data and financial calculations are available for review at the end of this report.

Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol
The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocols (IPMVP) are used to develop this 
report. The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), American Society of Heating, Refrigeration and 
Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and The Efficiency Valuation Organization (EVO) accept the 
IPMVP as a global methodology for determining the effectiveness of energy conservation methods and 
products.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize.  They 
are options A, B, C and D.  Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report.  Option B is 
defined as: All parameter measurements with the boundary of the ECM (PermaFrost NMR®) as the single 
source of measurement.  Savings are determined by field measurement of the energy use of the ECM 
affected equipment or system and any performance enhancements versus the baseline data.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period.  For the boundary utilized for Option B short-term 
measurements are very useful as data when the variables are contained.  The savings are calculated by 
short-term measurements of baseline and reporting period energy, and /or engineering computations using 
measurements of proxies of energy use. 
The final computation follows the formula:
Option B savings = Baseline Energy – Reporting Period Energy
+ - Routine adjustments + - Non-Routine Adjustments

Energy Conservation Method (ECM) Content
The content within the following report will demonstrate the ability of PermaFrost NMR® to correct the 
effects of thermal degradation and fouling on the heat exchange surfaces. 
The Company made the decision to treat two 16-ton CRAC units, both in good operating condition, 
supporting an isolated switching center within the facility.  A diagnostic examination of the pilot equipment 
was implemented to determine if the two units’ operational conditions were satisfactory.  Baseline 
measurements were recorded and then the proper amount and type of PermaFrost NMR® was injected. The 
product was then allowed four (4) weeks to seat itself into the metal surfaces before post measurements 
were taken to establish the efficiency gains. 
The following report produces the utilization of the IPMVP International Performance Measurement and 
Verification Protocol as the M&V plan.  The final calculations were performed by Powertron Global’s Senior 
Energy Engineer [Senior Energy Engineer] ME/CEM/CMC/CMVP.
The results were formulated by entering the data into the following thermodynamic engineering formulas:
 
kW = Volts X Amps x 1.56 (Three Phase) / 1000
 
Delta T = Return Air DB – Supply Air DB
 
Enthalpy = Return Air WB Deg. F and Supply Air WB Deg. F Converted to Enthalpy
 
Actual Btuh Capacity = Measured CFM X 4.5 * Enthalpy Delta 
 
System Eﬃciency % = Actual Coil Capacity Btuh / Nominal Coil Capacity Btuh
 
EER = Btuh / Watts

HVAC/R Efficiency Report (Preliminary) 
Purpose 
Thermal degradation is well documented by the American Society of Heating, Refrigeration and Air 
Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE) and the original equipment manufacturers (OEM’s). It is a major cause of 
capacity loss in Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration (HVACR) systems, preventing them 
from operating at the original design efficiency soon after installation.  The purpose of this study is to verify the 
effectiveness of the PermaFrost NMR® Energy Conservation Measure (ECM) in the European Chiller Manufacturer chiller #2 at the 
African Telecom Provider [[LOCATION REDACTED] Area] Switching Centre and document the future avoided energy costs associated with the same. 
Summary Results 
This report contains specific information regarding a chiller BASE and POST performance profile at 100% 
load supporting the African Telecom Provider A in South Africa.  BASE to POST performance versus design:  
•
95.51% to 90.31% less power consumed
•
76.91% to 88.61% increased cooling capacity
•
80.43% to 101.71% improved energy to capacity cost efficiency
•
80.48% to 98.51% improved coefficient of performance (COP)
All testing was conducted by HVAC Contractor B’s Managing Director and Director of Engineering, [Technical Director], 
assisted by Senior Technician [Client Representative], while being witnessed by [Client Representative], [Facilities Manager] and 
[Facilities Rep] of Facilities Management Company A plus [Client Representative] and [Client Representative] of African Telecom Provider.  
HVAC Contractor B supported the data collection process and installed the ECM into the chiller. HVAC Contractor B is the 
exclusive national distributor for European Chiller Manufacturer in South Africa.

reflected in the amount of kWEnergy per kWRefrigeration required measurement (kWE/kWR).
•
The thermal dynamic ability of the equipment to still perform at or close to operational design.

The testing measurements used in the efficiency calculations were collected and compiled in accordance 
with the IPMVP (International Measurement and Verification Protocol) framework.  The baseline day 
chosen to test the chiller was an average day temperature and humidity-wise for the Midrand area in the

PermaFrost NMR®

electrical disconnect for each machine or at each compressor in a dual-circuit 
HVAC unit where both compressors run an extensive amount of time annually.

Testing Methodologies
The team used two methods to capture the performance and energy use of the four CRAC systems. First, after 
verifying the amount of air ﬂowing across the evaporator coils before beginning each pilot, the subsequent 
measurements used in the efﬁciency calculations were collected and compiled in accordance with Option B of 
the IPMVP (International Measurement and Veriﬁcation Protocol). This Protocol was developed by experts in the 
international community and endorsed by the US Department of Energy to provide a consistent method for 
analyzing HVAC system performance. Baseline measurements were taken on November 11 with outside air 
temperatures averaging between 68-70 degrees. Post measurements were then taken in the same fashion on a 
similar weather day on December 16. 
The results presented below were formulated by entering the data into the following thermodynamic 
engineering formulas:
 
• kW = Volts * Amps * Power Factor * Sq Rt 3 /1000 (for 3-Phase) 
 
• kW/ton = Actual Measured Energy / Actual Measured Capacity 
 
• Coefﬁcient of Performance (COP) = 12 / (kW/ton) /3.412
 
• Actual Cooling Capacity per Hour = (Measured CFM * 4.5 * Enthalpy Delta T) / 12,000 BTU
The second method used to capture data involved installing a utility-grade power meter directly at the electrical 
panel housing only the breakers for the four pilot CRAC systems and the corresponding condensing units. The 
meter was installed on November 4 to capture one week of baseline prior to the ECM’s being installed on 
November 11. This data was then compared to data in the post (after PermaFrost NMR® had been in the systems 
for at least 250 runtime hours) in blocks of time when the weather was the same.

Explanation of Regression Analysis
To obtain a realistic avoided energy cost and subsequent payback period for Data Center Provider/Data Center REIT for implementing the PermaFrost NMR® and Circuit Master® 
ECMs, a detailed Regression Analysis is used to calculate the true energy savings resulting from the improvement in both capacity and efficiency 
utilizing data collected during the pilot study. Working together, these improvements reduce the annual kWh expended in the Post Analysis 
Period. The ROI comes from determining what the cost to run the cooling systems was when operating at the original energy profile to produce 
the newly restored amount of available capacity before then subtracting the revised cost to run the cooling systems at the same restored capacity 
after the ECMs were installed. This regression analysis is the most widely accepted method of accounting for the reduced number of hours and/or 
load % at which the systems will now operate due to the restored performance profile. This restored performance profile allows will normally allow 
the cooling systems to satisfy the internal area set points with increased efficiency resulting in reduced compressor demand loading.

HVAC/R Eﬃciency Report
Purpose of Energy Eﬃciency Study
The purpose of this study is to verify the industry wide problem of efficiency 
loss in HVAC/R as projected by ASHRAE research and to quantify the 
amount of money wasted due to this loss. Many industry leading 
organizations including ASHRAE project that all HVAC/R units degrade in 
capacity and efficiency as they age. Thermal degradation is caused by a 
phenomenon that is present in all HVACR equipment that operates as a 
vapor compression cycle associated with refrigerant and compressor lubricant. 
This thermal degradation is well documented by the HVACR industry and 
the original equipment manufacturers (OEM’s). Thermal degradation 
prevents units from operating at the original design efficiency, which leads to 
excessive run-times and additional kWh consumption.
The chiller in this study is representative of a great majority of the portfolio 
of equipment operated by Data Center Provider. If thermal degradation is present in this 
CRAC unit, it is present in the entire inventory of equipment. Energy waste 
can be calculated based on this unit (portfolio representation) and then 
accurately extrapolated across the entire inventory of equipment.

Energy Conservation Method (ECM)
The content detailed in this report will first demonstrate the ability of the pilot CRAC unit to perform prior to 
and following PermaFrost NMR® (ECM) being installed. The report will also illustrate the amount of thermal 
degradation that has occurred due in large part to thermal degradation within the heat exchangers and how much of 
that has been restored.
 
The following report produces the utilization of the IPMVP as the M&V plan. 
The results were formulated by entering the data into the following thermodynamic engineering formulas:
• kW = Volts * Amps * Power Factor of 1.47/1000 (for 3-Phase) 
• Tons = (Airflow * 4.5 * Enthalpy Delta) / 12,000 
• kW/Ton = kW / Actual Tonnage 
• Coefficient of Performance (COP) = (12 / kW per ton /3.412)
• Refrigerant Approach = Supply Air Temp – Saturated Suction Temp 
Notes 
Following a diagnostic examination of the pilot equipment to determine the operational condition of the system was 
satisfactory, Baseline M&V data was collected and recorded by the M&V team. Four hundred runtime hours after 
installation of PermaFrost NMR®, the M&V team returned on a very similar weather day to the Baseline to take Post 
M&V measurements in the identical fashion as in the Baseline. The delta of these measurements and associated 
calculations show the amount of capacity restored.
The following IPMVP data points were recorded on 5 May 2014 using recently calibrated devices by NIST (National 
Institutes of Standards and Technology) to insure measurement accuracy. The CRAC unit was then treated with

patented surface science nanotechnology had ample time to seat into all the metal surfaces of the heat exchangers. All 
measurements were taken at 100% load and at similar return air and outdoor air temperatures.

Purpose of Energy Eﬃciency Study
The purpose of this jointly-conducted ECM study between Data Center Provider (now owned by Data Center REIT) and PTG 
engineering teams was threefold. First, to verify the current as-is capacity and efficiency of 35 various 
Computer Room Air Conditioning (CRAC) systems supporting the five Data Center Provider data center suites within the 
[Commercial Building] located at [Building Address] in New York, NY. Second, to demonstrate what, if any, material 
performance changes occur in these same cooling units after being treated with PermaFrost NMR® ECM. And 
third, to determine what, if any, financial benefits are associated with any efficiency improvements realized.  
The identification of CRAC units involved in the study are recorded in Appendix A. 
ECM Product Brief
PermaFrost NMR® is a multi-patented surface science nanotechnology that uses Nucleo Molecular 
Regenerative (NMR®) technology as its core agent. A sustainable, one-time treatment with no down time 
required, PermaFrost NMR® lasts for the remaining life of any type of climate control system in which it is 
installed.  The direct benefits of PermaFrost NMR® are improved cooling efficiency and increased capacity, 
both of which result in lower overall costs to operate a system and extended equipment life.
Methodology
After determining the amount of air flowing across the evaporator coil was within 20% of manufacturer design 
(higher or lower) before beginning the testing of each unit, the subsequent measurements used in the efficiency 
calculations were collected and compiled in accordance with the IPMVP (International Measurement and 
Verification Protocol) framework. 
The results presented below were formulated by entering the data into the following thermodynamic 
engineering formulas:
• kW = (Volts * Amps * Power Factor of 1.47)/1000 (for 3-Phase) 
• kW/Ton = kW / Actual Tonnage 
• Coefficient of Performance (COP) = (12 / kW per ton /3.412)
• EER = Capacity in BTU’s / Power in Watts
• Actual Cooling Tons per Hour = (Measured CFM * 4.5 * Enthalpy Delta T) / 12,000 BTU

The Men’s Wearhouse Energy Eﬃciency Study
Purpose of Energy Eﬃciency Study
This efficiency study was conducted in an effort to verify the effectiveness of the PermaFrost NMR®  Energy 
Conservation Measure (ECM) in four large roof top units (RTUs) and a chiller at The Men’s Wearhouse (Retail Chain C) 
distribution facility and to document the future avoided energy costs associated with the same. These units 
represent a microcosm of the overall Retail Chain C portfolio of equipment. 
Understanding the Opportunity for Efficiency Restoration
All Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration (HVACR) systems experience thermal
degradation over time. Internal surfaces of heat exchangers lose their optimal thermal transfer
characteristics, resulting in reduced capacity, lower efficiency, and higher operating costs. This
degradation affects superheat levels and overall system performance, impacting the useful
equipment life of the HVACR system.
Restoring System Efficiency with PermaFrost NMR
PermaFrost NMR® technology addresses this thermal degradation by creating a permanent thermal
metal coating on the tube walls, whether on the inside or outside surfaces depending on the HVACR
equipment. This coating conditions the metal surfaces, reducing friction and restoring the system's
original thermal transfer efficiency. In every application this results in a lower per unit cost of cooling
which ultimately translates into lower overall energy costs.

Summary Results of Retail Chain C Study
This comprehensive report contains specific information regarding the performance profiles of four 25-ton 
Roof Top Units (RTUs) and one 140-ton air cooled chiller at Retail Chain C facility in [Texas City]. 
At the conclusion of the pilot, the five units showed the following substantial changes: 
 
• Overall capacity rose by 32.19 tons from 108.31 tons to 140.5 tons or 29.7%
 
• Average cost per unit of cooling (i.e., kW/ton) fell by .46 from 1.52 to 1.06 or 30.3%
 
• Aggregate kWh consumed based on avg kW/ton fell by 223,749 from 739,345 to 515,596 or 30.3% 
 
• Energy costs to operate the five units fell by $22,375 from $73,935 to $51,560 or 30.3%  
These efficiency improvements demonstrated equate to an Initial Payback Period (IPP) of the Retail Chain C project 
(including all testing fees) of 11.7 months and a corresponding Internal Rate of Return (IRR) of 103%. This is 
exactly what was estimated in the proposal given the age and average runtime of the equipment.
Further details of the measurements are described in the various sections later in this report. All testing was 
conducted by Powertron Global’s Director of Engineering, [Senior Energy Engineer] while being assisted and 
witnessed throughout by [Facility Manager] of Retail Chain C and his HVAC contractor, HVAC Services Provider.

Process
This comprehensive report contains specific information regarding the performance profiles of four of the 116 
packaged RTUs and one air-cooled chiller that support Retail Chain C facility in [Texas City]. 
Detailed performance testing (outlined later in this report) was performed on the units before (baseline) and 
after (post) the installation of the ECM. This testing determined the impact on three key elements relating to 
the original design specifications that greatly affect the HVAC portion of Retail Chain C power bill.  They include:
 
1. The cooling capacity the units are capable of producing after 11+ years in service. 
 
2. The actual cost of per unit of cooling the units are delivering as reflected in the kW/ton 
 
    measurement. 
 
3. The thermal dynamic ability of the equipment to still perform at or close to operational design.  
Methodology
The measurements used in the efficiency calculations were collected and compiled in accordance with the 
IPMVP (International Measurement and Verification Protocol) framework and the standards set forth by the 
National Environmental Balancing Bureau (NEBB).
 
Powertron Global’s Director of Engineering, [Senior Energy Engineer] took and recorded all of the readings while 
being assisted and witnessed by HVAC Services Provider technicians during every phase of the testing.  
The collection periods for each of the units were similar in both the baseline and post periods to best replicate 
internal building loads.

Energy Conservation Method (ECM)
The content detailed in this report will first demonstrate the ability of the pilot chiller to perform prior to 
PermaFrost NMR® (ECM) being installed, as well as illustrate the amount of thermal degradation due in large 
part to thermal degradation within the heat exchangers (evaporator and condenser barrels).
 
The following report produces the utilization of the IPMVP as the M&V plan. 
The results were formulated by entering the data into the following applicable thermodynamic 
engineering formulas:
 
• kW = Volts * Amps * Power Factor of 1.47/1000 (for 3-Phase) 
 
• Ton = (Airflow * 4.5 * Enthalpy Delta) / 12,000 
 
• kW/Ton = kW / Actual Tonnage 
 
• Coefficient of Performance (COP) = (12 / kW per ton /3.412)
 
• Actual Cooling Tons per Hour = Evaporator GPM X 8.34 * 60 * Chilled Water Delta T / 12,000 BTU 
 
• Refrigerant Approach = Supply Water Temp – Saturated Evaporator Temp (CH)

Engineering Notes
Following a diagnostic examination of the pilot equipment to determine the operational condition of the units were 
satisfactory, Baseline M&V data was collected and recorded by the M&V team with assistance from HVAC Services Provider. Units 
51 and 52 were initially tested and treated on 16 July 2014 and had 400+ runtime hours after installation of the ECM 
before the post readings were taken on 25 Sept 2014. Due to some maintenance and scheduling issues, units 50 and 57 
were not initially tested and treated until 14 Aug 2014 and had just over 300 runtime hours while the chiller, which was 
also tested and treated on 14 Aug, had just under 250 runtime hours on it when post readings were taken on 25 Sept 
2014. Since the combined results were well within expected savings parameters, no further readings are necessary.  
Both the baseline dates were nearly identical weather and building load perspective. The scheduled post reading date was 
somewhat cooler but the internal building load was the same in three of the spaces served by the units. To replicate 
similar weather conditions on the RTUs, doors were opened to the compressors to get the head pressures to close to what 
they were in the baseline readings. Any shortfalls in pressures were adjusted for by raising the post amps accordingly. 
Due to differences in operational load, the area served by unit 50 was above the 1 degree entering air WB temperature 
difference testing parameters we normally accept to assure high confidence in the data but the team decided to leave it a 
part of the study for transparency. The load on circuit B of the chiller was much higher in the post (86.5%) than in the 
baseline (50%) and since circuit A was still down for maintenance the M&V team could not load limit the chiller to take 
measurements without negatively affecting laundry operations. For this portion of the test the key element to look at is the 
reduction of kW/ton. 
As expected in any in-situ testing, all the RTUs had varying airflows, refrigerant temps and enthalpy deltas which show 
up in the varying levels of performance. This is the reason to focus on the delta improvements both at each unit and as an 
aggregate. 
The collection of the data in both the baseline and post periods was collected by Powertron Global® while witnessed 
throughout by HVAC Services Provider technicians. Pictures were also taken of all the key readings used in the formulas and are 
available upon request.

Calculated Capacity of Retail Chain C Units Baseline and Post
The charts below illustrate just how far off Retail Chain C units had degraded in terms of capacity over 11+ years of use. 
With the RTUs operating at 100% load and the chiller at 50% load (adjusted down from 87% in post), these  
same five pilot units were determined in the baseline measurement periods to be producing a total of 108.31 
tons of cooling out of a possible 135 nominal design tons. This represents 80.2% of nominal design capacity. The 
majority of this capacity loss is directly attributable to the thermal degradation of the heat exchange surfaces 
over time. This is due in large part to thermal degradation which creates an insulating barrier to heat transfer on the 
tube walls. 
After the PermaFrost NMR® ECM was installed and allowed to work inside the units for an average of 300+ 
runtime hours, the average total capacity of the five pilot units rose 32.19 tons to 140.5 tons or 104% of the 
overall nominal design capacity of all five units. This represents a 29.7% increase in nominal capacity over the 
baseline numbers.

systems will now operate due to the restored capacity. This restored capacity allows the systems to reach the internal 
building set points with increased efficiency resulting in reduced compressor demand loading.

Purpose of Study 
 
The purpose of this study is twofold.  First, to verify the current capacity and efficiency of a seven-year 
old packaged roof top unit (RTU) in relation to original equipment manufacturer (OEM) design 
specifications.  Second, to demonstrate what, if any, material changes occur in this same unit after 
being treated with PermaFrost NMR.   
 
The identification of test unit is recorded as follows: 
 
2008 HVAC Equipment Manufacturer, 7.5 Ton, R-22, 208/230 Volt-3 Phase, Model TSC090A3EGAZUB 
 
 
Preparation of the Unit for Testing 
 
Powertron Global delivered the test sample equipment to the UL test lab located at [LOCATION REDACTED]. Suite 
200, [Texas Location], Texas.   
UL unloaded and uncrated the test sample equipment and recorded all nameplate information, 
compressors, condenser fan motors, and the type and size of the evaporator and condenser coils.  
UL witnessed and/or took part in the preparation of the units in the staging area by the mechanical 
contractor, Lane Valente Refrigeration (LVR) before separately taking the unit into the test chamber. 
This included the following: 
-­‐ 
all heating elements and economizers being removed so as not to affect the test data (LVR) 
-­‐ 
refrigerant being recovered into its own vessel (LVR) 
-­‐ 
refrigerant being tested for acid content (LVR) 
-­‐ 
core driers being replaced to reduce the chance of creating a restriction during testing (LVR) 
-­‐ 
vacuum being pulled on the system down to 500 microns  for 30 minutes (LVR) 
-­‐ 
reclaimed refrigerant being reinstalled per nameplate (LVR) 
-­‐ 
external coils being inspected for cleanliness (LVR) 
-­‐ 
particulate return air filters being removed during the test (LVR) 
 
Testing Procedures 
After complete mechanical servicing and preparations, the test sample was installed inside the AHRI 
certified dual psychometric environmental test chamber. Next, the indoor and outdoor ductwork was 
built according to ASHRAE 37-2009 and installed on the test sample.  Transducers were then installed 
on the refrigerant lines to measure refrigerant pressures. Thermocouples were installed to provide 
refrigerant line temperatures for the purpose of calculating superheat. Airflow was measured and 
verified within 5% of a rate of 400 CFM per ton. The measurement methodology for air-flow included 
utilizing a NIST certified hot wire anemometer as defined per ASHRAE 37-2009 section

Conclusion 
 
Upon detailed examination in a controlled chamber, the baseline measurements determined that the 
test unit showed a considerable amount of degraded capacity and efficiency loss per OEM design 
specifications.  
Following the baseline readings, 8 ounces of PermaFrost NMR (corresponding to nominal equipment 
design tonnage of the test unit) was injected into the evaporator section of the test unit while under load 
inside the controlled chamber. The test unit was then removed from the chamber and installed into a 
holding chamber where it was allowed to run at full load for 400+ hours. According to the OEM, this 
was the approximate amount of time the PermaFrost NMR chemical compound required to fully 
displace the lubricant from the metal surfaces of the heat exchangers and then absorb into these same 
metal surfaces to prevent a reoccurrence of the thermal inefficiency condition.  
Subsequent to the 400+ hours of run time, the test unit was then reinserted into the test chamber to 
allow for data collection and analysis. The system showed a significant increase in capacity compared 
to the baseline.  With this increase in capacity came an equally significant improvement in efficiency of 
the test unit as measured in EER and condensate collected.

Technical Narrative
This reports contains the details regarding the installation of PermaFrost NMR™ in chiller #1 of the US Navy Vessel 
Benavidez.  PermaFrost NMR® is a chemical designed to correct the issue of thermal inefficiency in HVACR 
equipment. 
The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP) was used to develop this 
report.  The Association of Energy Engineers (AEE), American Society of Heating, Refrigeration and 
Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and The Efficiency Valuation Organization (EVO) accept the IPMVP 
as a global standard.
There are four distinct options in the IPMVP protocol for energy conservation professionals to utilize. 
Retrofit Isolation (Option B) was the option used for this report.
Retrofit Isolation (Option B) is defined as: All parameter measurement.  Savings are determined by field 
measurement of the energy use of the energy conservation method affected equipment or system.
Measurement frequency ranges from short term to continuous, depending on the expected variations in the 
savings and the length of the reporting period.  The savings are calculated by short term or continuous 
measurements of baseline and reporting period energy, and /or engineering computations using 
measurements of proxies of energy use. 
The final computation follows the formula:

System Description / Design Characteristics
The chilled water distribution plant of The US Navy Vessel Benavidez is equipped with five York centrifugal chillers. 
Each chiller is equipped with a chilled water centrifugal pump feeding a common header. The two chillers 
in this report are indentical make and model with approximately 1.6 years of runtime.
  
The fresh water-cooled condensers of these chillers are fed from a central fresh water loop that is cooled via 
plate and frame heat exchangers utilizing seawater as the heat exchange / rejection medium. Operational 
conditions are distinctly different when the vessel is docked versus when at sea. The results of this report are 
predicated on operation while docked. The air conditioning plant while docked only has the ability to 
operate one chiller at a time. This is due to the reduced fresh water flow provided by the in port central fresh 
water circulating pump. While docked many of the large square foot areas cooled by the energy plant are 
non-active. Areas that are active are living quarters, bridge and other areas required for the daily non 
-commissioned activities of this vessel. 
The cooling coils that are served by this chilled water 
distribution system are controlled by two-way solenoid 
valves. Upon satisfaction of the temperature requirements 
of the conditioned space these valves will close until the 
space temperature rises. 
At the time of this performance verification the vessel was 
docked and one chiller was being utilized. This IPMVP Plan 
was developed with a defined measurement boundary. That boundary is comprised of Chiller #1 and 
Chiller #5. This boundary was selected with the assistance of the ship’s Chief Engineer [Client Representative]. Chiller 
#1 and #5 are both York Codepak Model YKM2M2G4-CBS Centrifugal water-cooled chillers each rated at 330 
tons equipped with R-134a refrigerant. 
Each chiller was subjected to identical performance parameters demonstrated by the local control of the 
incremental loading of each chiller within a controlled parameter. The verification process was initiated and 
concluded on two consecutive days.  Each day began with no chillers running. One chilled water pump was 
operating in an effort to increase the load on the chilled water loop to a maximum of 80 deg. F.

Baseline Measurement Period Selection
Chiller #1 was treated with PermaFrost NMR® on Q3 2011.  There was a pre and post measurement 
and verification performed to develop a baseline to determine the efficacy of this energy conservation 
measure that consisted of chiller #1 (unit treated with PermaFrost NMR®) and chiller #5 (no PermaFrost 
NMR® treatment). 
Each chiller was started and limited to the load factor of 80% by limiting the inlet guide vane position of the 
machines for a period of five minutes.  During this five-minute period the following parameters were 
recorded:
Chiller kW, Chilled Water Delta T, Condenser Water Delta T, Condensed Liquid Refrigerant Temperature, 
Saturated Evaporator Refrigerant Temperature, Actual Tonnage and kW per Ton.
The results were formulated by entering the data into thermodynamic engineering formulas.
These formulas are as follows:
• To determine the kW, voltage, amperage and power factor were recorded using a digital kW meter.  Data 
from that meter is automatically calculated.  Those data streams were verified by the manual calculation for 
determining kW energy as:
 
Volts X Amps X .85 X 1.73 / 1000 = kW
• To determine the tonnage the following formula was utilized:
 
GPM X 8.34 X 60 X Chilled Water Delta T / 12,000 BTU = Actual Tonnage
• To determine the actual kW per ton the following formula was utilized:
 
Actual kW / Actual Tonnage = kW per Ton

Conclusion
The improved efficiency (kW per ton) at the unit at 80% load was 9.4% with and additional 3.8% increase 
in capacity.  The improvement in the refrigerant approach, a measurable thermodynamic enhancement 
of PermaFrost NMR®, at 80% load was 53%.  These results are highly significant.  Chiller #1 not only 
provides chilled water at the rated GPM and design chilled water outlet temperature at reduced kW-hr and 
cost, it also does this at a greater tonnage per kW.  This allows the chiller to produce more tonnage at less 
energy. 
These results are in line with what we would expect on a chiller that has only 1.6 years of actual runtime. 
According to ASHRAE, thermal inefficiency of the heat transfer surfaces of air conditioning and refrigeration 
systems, will cause a loss of about 7% efficiency the first year, 5% the second year, and 2% per year the 
following years.  This loss will continue to accumulate until equilibrium is reached between flow force and 
adhesion.  At this point the thermal boundary layer formed has achieved its maximum thickness, producing 
maximum loss of efficiency.  Published ASHRAE information confirms these observations.  According to 
ASHRAE, performance is degraded by as much as 30% due to the thermal degradation of internal 
surfaces.  Higher percentages up to 40% have been observed in systems 20 years old or older.
These identical units (Chiller #1 & #5) have approximately 1.6 years of actual runtime, which equates to a 
loss of efficiency of 9.6% according to the above thermal inefficiency rates from ASHRAE. The efficiency 
improvement on Chiller #1 is 9.4%, which puts these results in line with a ASHRAE.  Now that Chiller #1 
has been treated with PermaFrost NMR®, the efficiency has been restored and the heat exchange surfaces 
are now protected from thermal inefficiency reoccurring for the life of the unit.
Chiller number one, treated with PermaFrost NMR®, has produced significant results.  Additionally, there 
are several direct benefits and indirect benefits that increase the return on investment but may not be easily 
measured.  These additional direct and indirect benefits are as follows:

HVAC/R Eﬃciency Report
Purpose of Energy Eﬃciency Study
The purpose of this study is to verify the industry wide problem of efficiency loss in HVAC/R systems as 
projected by ASHRAE research and to quantify the amount of money wasted due to this loss. Many industry 
leading organizations including ASHRAE project that all HVAC/R systems degrade in capacity and efficiency 
as they age. Thermal degradation is caused by a phenomenon that is present in all HVAC/R equipment that 
operates as a vapor compression cycle associated with refrigerant and compressor lubricant. This thermal 
degradation is well documented by the HVAC/R industry and the original equipment manufacturers (OEM’s). 
Thermal degradation prevents systems from operating at the original design efficiency, which leads to excessive 
run-times and additional kWh consumption.
The chiller in this study is representative of a great majority of the portfolio of data center and central office 
equipment operated by Major US Telecom. If thermal degradation is present in this chiller, it is present in the entire 
inventory of equipment. Energy waste can be calculated based on this equipment (portfolio representation) and 
then accurately extrapolated across the entire inventory of equipment.
Similarly, if the lost efficiency of this chiller can 
be restored, it would allow Major US Telecom to keep it in 
service longer without sacrificing performance 
or energy consumption. It will also provide 
Major US Telecom the flexibility of a much wider window 
of time wherein to undertake the costly capital 
expense of replacing this and other HVAC/R 
systems when they do eventually reach the end 
of their useful life.

Methodology
The measurements used in the efficiency calculations were collected and compiled in accordance with the IPMVP 
(International Measurement and Verification Protocol) framework using both instantaneous power reading and 
long term power readings with the chiller performing under similar operational and load conditions. 
The M&V team was led by [Client Representative] of [Client Representative] Associates, with support from [Senior Energy Engineer], 
Director of Engineering for Powertron Global®. Major US Telecom personnel overseeing the pilot and supporting the 
M&V team on site included [Special Projects Manager], [Sr. Facility Engineer] and [Facilities Engineer]. The overall project was managed and 
directed by [Facility Manager], Sr. Program Manager for Major US Telecom Corporate Special Projects.  
 
Notes 
Both the baseline and post readings were taken at 49% load with incoming condenser water within a degree of 78 degrees 
and incoming chilled water at 53 degrees, therefore no adjustments were made to the resulting data. Major US Telecom’s 
management of the chiller plant combined with the building load during the trial provided more than an adequate heat load 
on the facility to ensure the chiller would remain running during the actual data collection period.  
The chiller was tested over the span of three weeks while operating at an average of 49% motor load. This is the minimum 
amount of time the PermaFrost NMR® ECM requires in a chiller of this size to produce maximum results, therefore 
Major US Telecom can expect to continue to see continued improvements over the next month. The boundary of the testing was the 
chiller and nothing else therefore confidence in the accuracy of the performance calculations is very high.

Energy Conservation Method (ECM)
The content detailed in this report will first demonstrate the ability of the pilot chiller to perform prior to the 
PermaFrost NMR® (ECM) being installed, as well as illustrate the amount of thermal degradation due in large 
part to thermal degradation within the heat exchangers (evaporator and condenser barrels).  
The following report lists the results of using the IPMVP as the M&V plan. 
The results were formulated by entering the data into the following applicable thermodynamic engineering 
formulas:
 
• kW = Volts * Amps * Power Factor of 1.47/1000 (for 3-Phase) 
 
• kW/Ton = kW / Actual Tonnage 
 
• Coefficient of Performance (COP) = (12 / kW per ton /3.412)
 
• Actual Cooling Tons per Hour = Evaporator GPM X 8.34 * 60 * Chilled Water Delta T / 12,000 BTU 
 
• Refrigerant Approach = Supply Water Temp – Suction Temp of Evaporator (CH)

Product Brief
         PermaFrost NMR® is a multi-patented nanotechnology surface science Energy Control Measure 
(ECM) that uses Nucleo Molecular Regenerative (NMR) technology as its core agent.  A sustainable, 
one-time treatment with no down time required, PermaFrost NMR® lasts for the remaining life of any 
type of system in which it is installed – DX (direct expansion air and chilled water systems), Chillers 
(screw, reciprocating, scroll and centrifugal), heat pumps, ice making equipment.  Specialized 
applications include computer room cooling and dehumidification systems, chiller plants (water and ice 
production applications), domestic and industrial refrigeration (ammonia low and ultra low 
temperature), air-cooled single application water chillers and split and package rooftop HVAC 
equipment.
The direct benefits of PermaFrost NMR® are improved cooling performance, increased capacity, and 
improved refrigerant velocity – all of which allows a system to achieve set point temperatures in a more 
rapid fashion that reduces system loading and operating periods.  The indirect benefits resulting from 
the enhanced thermodynamic characteristics following treatment include reduced run time, less kW 
hours used, less amp draw at the compressor, less metallic wear and longer overall equipment life.

Executive Summary
This report contains specific information regarding the installation of PermaFrost NMR® in the 54-ton 
Carrier Water Cooled DX Unit #1 at the Commercial Real Estate Company Bldg at [Commercial Address], NYC.  The facility houses the 
Traffic Police Department for the City of New York.  Unit #1 is owned and maintained by Commercial Real Estate Company located 
in New York, NY.  Louis Rojo, Commercial Real Estate Company Facility Manager for this location, oversaw the trial. 
The improved/restored efficiency on the unit directly attributable to the PermaFrost NMR® ECM was 
substantial.  The unit now provides cooler supply air with greater efficiency due to the restoration of the 
heat transfer capacity of the evaporator and condenser coils and increased the available useful tonnage. 
All three compressors were operating within design/operating standards and very similar to one another 
and all outside air dampers were closed both pre and post.
The overall system efficiency improved by 17.8% and the EER improved by 42.8%.  There was an increase in 
coil capacity of 96,525 in Btuh which equates to gaining 8-tons of capacity or 17.8%.  There is also a 
reduction of 18% in total power and watts per ton which is another measurable way to view the 
thermodynamic enhancement of the PermaFrost NMR® ECM.  The tables of data and financial calculations 
are available for review at the end of this report.  The result of these combined ECM improvements is an 
ROI to Commercial Real Estate Company of 23.9 months.

Utilizing the data in the above charts, the following steps were taken to determine a very accurate ROI for 
Commercial Real Estate Company for implementing this ECM:
Baseline kWh = (59,155 NTW / 1,000) * 1,500 Annual Operating Hrs = 88,733 kWh
Baseline Cost To Run = 88,733 kWh * $.18 = $15,972
Regression Analysis is then used to account for amount of tonnage restored to Unit #1
Adjusted Base Tonnage = 53.21 tons (equates to tonnage in ERP) 
Adjusted Total Watts = 1,310 WPT * 53.21 tons = 69,705 W
Adjusted Base kWh = (69,705 W/1,000) * 1,500 Annual Operating Hrs = 104,558 kWh
Revised Cost to Run Prior to ECM = 104,558 kWh * $.18 = $18,820
Post ECM kWh = (57,183 W / 1,000) * 1,500 Annual Operating Hrs = 85,775 kWh
Cost to Run After ECM = 85,775 kWh * $.18 = $15,440
Cost Savings per Month = ($18,820 - $15,440) / 12 = $282
Cost of PermaFrost NMR® installed @ $6,750 / $282 = 23.9 months
 
ROI = 23.9 months

Purpose of Energy Eﬃciency Study
Thermal degradation is well documented by the American Society of Heating, Refrigeration and Air 
Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE) and the original equipment manufacturers (OEM’s). It is a major cause of 
capacity loss in Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration (HVACR) systems, preventing them 
from operating at the original design efficiency soon after initial installation in the field. 
The purpose of this study is to verify the effectiveness of the PermaFrost NMR® Energy Conservation Measure 
(ECM) in a water-cooled DX Chiller unit (pictured below) at the African Telecom Provider B switching center location and 
document the future avoided energy costs associated with the same.

Process
This comprehensive report contains specific information regarding the performance profile of a single 
water-cooled DX chiller (DXC) that supports the African Telecom Provider B facility. The detailed performance testing 
(outlined later in this report) was performed on the DXC before (baseline) and after (post) the installation of
